code.title: Entire retention loop (review schedule, strength, completion flags, pre-test) lives only in localStorage; the one server write fails silently
code.fix: Persist completion, review schedule and strength server-side keyed by user_id (a small user_section_state table: completed_at, review_interval_idx, next_due, reviews, quiz_accuracy, pretest_score, pretest_questions). Fix or delete /api/learn-mode/progress: either change last_result to TEXT or stop writing strings; check the upsert error and return 500 so the failure is visible. Hydrate localStorage from the server on login as a cache, not the source of truth.
code.impact: A student who completes a topic on their school laptop and opens Revvy on their phone (or in incognito, or after Safari's 7-day ITP storage eviction, or after clearing site data) has: no completion dot in the sidebar, no strength bar, no scheduled reviews, no pre-test record, and the section re-opens at the DB-saved step with the pre-test gate suppressed only because isResuming is true. The 1/3/7/14-day spaced review promise is broken for anyone who is not on the exact same browser profile every time. Logged-in status changes nothing.
code.evidence: app/api/learn-mode/state/route.js:78-101 reads existing row before upsert so a partial write can't blank other fields; lib/section-state.js:29-40 migrates legacy revvy_complete_/revvy_pretest_ keys on first read; saveSectionState (section-state.js:82-99) writes local first and no-ops safely on 401 signed-out; GET returns {state:{},signedIn:false} when signed out (curl-verified) and {unavailable:true} rather than 500 when the table errors (route.js:58-64)

code.title: Nothing ever brings a student back for a due review; the only 'review due' banner is hidden on the screens a returning student actually lands on
code.fix: Surface due learn-mode reviews on HomeScreen and on the CompletionScreen itself ('Your review of this topic is due tomorrow at ...'). Once the schedule is server-side, add a daily email/push digest of due reviews. Also render the banner above the pre-test gate and completion screen, not just the step view.
code.impact: Day 1 after completing 'introductory-concepts', a student re-opens the app. Every section change lands on the Learn tab; if they open the section they finished, they see the Completion screen (no banner). If they open a new section they first hit the pre-test gate (no banner). Only once they are inside the step view of an unfinished section do they see '1 review due'. Nobody outside the app is told; the review exists only if the student stumbles into it.

code.title: Explain It Back always reads 0/1 with an empty bar on every completion screen because the attempt callback is never wired
code.fix: Pass onExplainAttempt into ExplainItBackUpgraded and call it on submit (or on graded result for premium). Hide the Explain row when total is 0, and hide the 20% weight label unless a composite score is actually computed and shown.
code.impact: Every student who answers at least one quiz or recall sees a 'Score Breakdown' in which 'Explain It Back 0/1' sits with an empty bar and a 20% weight, regardless of whether they wrote three paragraphs and got AI feedback. It reads as 'you failed this' or 'the app is broken'. Free users, who cannot get their explanation graded, are told they scored 0 on a component they were never allowed to complete.
code.evidence: components/LearnModeTab.jsx:83-86 onExplainAttempt wired to both ExplainItBackUpgraded instances (lines 473,515); components/learn-mode/CompletionScreen.jsx:94-101 row hidden when total=0, weight labels removed; components/learn-mode/ExplainItBackUpgraded.jsx:16-22 free users counted via onBlur (line 81), premium via handleGrade (line 40)

code.title: Strength meter maths guarantee a completed topic is amber on the completion screen, red within 2 days, ~11% after a week
code.fix: Rebase the model: completion should land at a clearly positive value (e.g. 70-80) and decay should follow the scheduled interval (strength hits the 'review' threshold roughly when the review is due, not two days in). Feed inline quiz correctness, post-test and quick-fire results into quizAccuracy. Show 'Review due in N days' rather than a decaying percentage on the completion screen. Do not show a decaying bar in the sidebar next to a completion dot.
code.impact: The first thing under 'Topic complete' is an amber bar saying '35% strength'. Coming back tomorrow it is 30%, then red. A student who completes five topics in a week sees a sidebar full of red slivers next to every green completion dot. The 14-day review interval the app schedules is incompatible with its own meter: by the time the review is due the meter says <10% even after a perfect previous review. Nothing the student does inside Learn Mode (inline quiz, explain-it-back, recalls, quick-fire, post-test) raises the meter except a SpacedReview or MixedReview.
code.evidence: components/Sidebar.jsx:6 the StrengthMeter import is gone and 150-177 renders one status glyph only, so no decaying bar sits beside the completion dot anywhere in the sidebar; the new due state is derived in a mount effect at Sidebar.jsx:29-40 (getStrengthData + nextReviewAt) with an empty Set as initial state, so nothing reads localStorage during render and no hydration mismatch is possible (app/globals.css:417 styles .due; localhost:3001 console clean, no hydration warning). Residuals recorded, not blocking: CompletionScreen.jsx:106 still prints the percentage next to the date (StrengthMeter.jsx:53 renders n% strength - review in N days) rather than the date alone, and inline-quiz correctness still never reaches quizAccuracy (LearnModeTab.jsx:309 calls recordReview with null; only the drill/post-test at CompletionScreen.jsx:44-46 and ReviewMode do), so the sidebar due flag at nextReviewAt can also lead the 1/3/7/14 schedule written at LearnModeTab.jsx:302 by roughly half an interval

code.title: Post-test and Quick Fire results are discarded: they never affect strength, the review schedule, or the server
code.fix: On post-test and drill completion, call recordReview(subjectId, sectionId, score) and (once server-side) update the schedule: a strong post-test could push the first review from 1 day to 3.
code.impact: A student who does the post-test and goes 1/3 -> 3/3 sees 'Perfect score! You've mastered this topic', then the strength meter above it still says 35% and tomorrow's review is still due. Effort in the optional activities has no visible consequence anywhere else in the app.
code.evidence: PostTest.jsx:43-49 and QuickFireDrill.jsx:110-114 each report onScore exactly once via a reportedRef guard; both wired to CompletionScreen.jsx:43-47 handleDrillScore, which calls recordReview() and saveSectionState({quizAccuracy, reviewed}) at lines 45-46, reaching strength.js and the server schedule

code.title: Score Breakdown is component state: it disappears on revisit and double-counts on Retry; weights 50/30/20 label a composite that is never computed
code.fix: Persist per-attempt scores with the completion record; reset scores in onRetry; drop the weight labels or compute and display the composite; require at least 3 quiz answers before the 'needs attention' callout.
code.impact: First time: a breakdown with 'Quiz 0/1 50%' and a warning 'Quiz questions need attention' after a single wrong click. Tomorrow: the same screen with no breakdown at all. After Retry: 'Quiz 1/2' even though they answered the single question right the second time. The percentages imply a mastery score the app never calculates.
code.evidence: components/learn-mode/CompletionScreen.jsx:128-153 gates the weakest-area callout on MIN_ANSWERS=3 and WEAK_BELOW=0.7 (filter on a.s.total >= MIN_ANSWERS at line 141), so one wrong answer out of one can no longer produce a verdict; it now ranks quiz against recall by accuracy and names the worse of the two with the raw count. Persistence and retry reset already stood: LearnModeTab.jsx:99-101 seeds scores from readLocalState, :292 writes them with the completion record, :364-366 resets a fresh zeroed object on Retry; weight labels gone at CompletionScreen.jsx:107-110. code.title: Recall score counts only attempted widgets; dismissing with the x is invisible
code.fix: Report skips to the parent (onComplete(null) or an onSkip prop) and show 'Recall 1 of 10 attempted, 1 correct'; de-duplicate by recall prompt so the spaced re-attempt updates rather than appends.
code.impact: Skip nine reorders, check one: 'Recall 1/1' with a full bar. Do the same fill-in twice: 2/2. The number is technically not false but it does not measure what the label implies.

code.title: Same MCQ bank is reused for pre-test, inline quiz, spaced review (identical 5 forever), quick fire, and the Quiz tab; pre-test reveals the answers first
code.fix: Do not reveal correct answers on the pre-test (score only, or reveal after completion). Partition the bank: reserve questions not used in pre-test/inline for reviews, and re-sample review questions from the section at each interval rather than freezing them at completion. Retire an entry after the 14-day pass or extend to 30/60 days.
code.impact: A section with 8 MCQs: the student sees three of them (with answers revealed) before learning, sees them again inline, again in the post-test, again in quick fire, again in the Quiz tab, and the same 5 every 1, 3, 7, 14, 14, 14... days. 'Improvement' on the post-test mostly measures having seen the green highlight 20 minutes earlier. Reviews become answer-recognition, not retrieval.
code.evidence: CONFIRMED. Both rejected sub-clauses are closed, verified live on dev 3001 at 390px against a served bundle re-read from the page (isDue, the MixedReview write-back and the post-test retry are all present in the delivered chunks, describesOption is not, so no stale JSX). (1) ONE DUE PREDICATE. ReviewMode.jsx:46-48 isDue(entry,now) = !!entry && !entry.retired && entry.nextDue <= now, used by countDueReviews (:52) and getDueReviews (:63) and by nothing else; both forms confirmed in the served bundle, not just the source. Live with two retired overdue entries plus one non-retired overdue entry the banner read '1 review due' and 'Review now' opened the Spaced Review for the non-retired topic (Live Gamma) - count, button and list all agree, and the non-retired due topic is still offered. With ONLY the two retired overdue entries the banner does not render at all: no number, no dead control. NO THIRD ROUTE: revvy_review_schedule is read in exactly three places - ReviewMode.jsx:21, LearnModeTab.jsx:308 (write) and CompletionScreen.jsx:54, and the last is .length for the 'Mixed review (N topics)' CTA, not a due count. HomeScreen/ProgressDashboard overdueCount comes from app/api/progress/dashboard/route.js:181-186 over server per-question SM-2 rows and never reads this schedule; lib/spaced-repetition.js is the practice engine's own queue. (2) RETIREMENT IS REVERSIBLE. ReviewMode.jsx:297-321. Live, mixed review scored 0/9 across two retired and one never-retired entry: both retired entries came back retired true->false, currentInterval 5->4, nextDue +30d, lastScore 0; the never-retired entry was byte-identical afterwards, so the guard at :308 (score >= 0.6 || !entry.retired) cannot resurrect a topic that was never retired. Entry stays valid for every other reader: the ...entry spread kept questions, intervals [1,3,7,14,30,60], title, subjectId and optionsShuffled, and reviewsDone is deliberately unchanged so SpacedReview's window (:137) does not jump. A GOOD mixed review does not advance: 9/9 on the same fixture left revvy_review_schedule byte-identical (retired still true, currentInterval 5, nextDue delta 0) while recordReview still fired. QUOTA: with Storage.prototype.setItem made to throw for revvy_review_schedule only, a 0/6 mixed review left the schedule unchanged (1 write blocked, swallowed by the bare catch at :123) but revvy_strength_1_retired-alpha and _live-gamma were both written (reviews 1, quizAccuracy 0) and the result screen rendered with no React error - recordReview at :301 runs inside the loop, saveSchedule at :321 after it, so the strength write cannot be lost to a schedule quota failure. REACHABILITY, residual not blocking: MixedReview has exactly two entry points - the Learn banner (LearnModeTab.jsx:453, gated on dueReviews > 0, so unreachable when everything is retired) and CompletionScreen.jsx:215, gated on completedCount >= 3. Verified live that the second works: with 3 retired topics and nothing due, 'Mixed review (3topics)' appeared on the completion screen and a 0/9 run un-retired all three. But with exactly 2 scheduled topics, both retired, there is no banner and no mixed control anywhere, so for a student with fewer than 3 completed sections retirement is still one-way. Narrow (a topic needs 55+ days of correct reviews to retire) and the student sees an honest zero rather than a wrong number, so not held against the finding. Also still true and pre-existing: saveSchedule's failure is entirely silent to the student. AST sweep over all 34 changed .js/.jsx in 1c98d69^..a11f3e6 clean for TDZ reads, hooks after a conditional return and used-but-unimported identifiers; checker validated by reproducing 163fd01 LearnModeTab.jsx:363 TDZ, 526f4e4 PostTest.jsx:63-64 hooks and 163fd01 PracticeEngine.jsx:347 missing useEffect import. Console over the whole walkthrough: only pre-existing signed-out 401s and umami CSP/CORS noise.

code.fix: Record the skip (e.g. { skipped: true, timestamp }) so the gate is shown once; consider making the pre-test opt-in ('Want to test what you know first?') rather than a gate, and offer the post-test from a fresh sample when no pre-test exists.

code.title: Home 'Mastery', 'Streak', 'This Week' and /progress ignore Learn Mode, Quiz tab and Flashcards tab entirely
code.fix: Define one mastery model that ingests Learn Mode inline quiz/recall results, Quiz tab attempts and Flashcards tab reviews alongside Smart Practice; compute streak from any learning activity (including user_content_progress.updated_at); until then, hide the Mastery/Streak tiles for users with no practice rows rather than showing zeros.

code.evidence: RE-CONFIRMED after the approach changed (bare bracketed letters are no longer rewritten at all; describesOption and the symbolic pre-scan are deleted - grep finds neither anywhere in app/, components/, lib/, scripts/). Independent scanner rerun over all 43 audit/content-sections/*.json, 769 questions, with a FORCED DERANGEMENT oldToNew[i]=(i+1)%n driven through the exported remapOptionLetters: my own raw-char standalone A-F detector, my own bracket-depth counter and my own backwards keyword-list walker, no tokeniser or rule shared with lib/shuffle-options.js. Results: 744 shuffled, 25 declined, 89 explanations changed, 262 letters moved, and 0 references pointing at a different option, 0 duplicated letters, 0 length changes, 0 characters changed outside a single A-F swap, 0 swaps that are not the derangement image. Correct-answer TEXT unchanged for all 769 through shuffleOptions, and the option multiset is preserved in every shuffled question. Stale census over the 744 shuffled: 421 standalone A-F letters, 262 claimed as keyword-list references and all 262 moved, 0 bare-bracketed, 0 bracketed-but-not-alone, 159 loose - and of those 159 ZERO are inside brackets and ZERO are within six words of option/answer/statement, so no missed reference remains. Distribution A4.8/B64.0/C28.5/D2.7 -> A25.6/B24.1/C24.6/D25.7 under the live salt, so the best blind single-letter guess falls from 64.0% to 25.7% against a 25% floor. Non-references still stay: 'Plan B', 'Grade A', 'A rise in income', 'from A to B', 'the options available to a firm', and the documented 'Option A describes area B only' (A moves, the Lorenz area B does not). MY PREVIOUS FOOLING CASE NOW DECLINES: options[2]='Consumer spending rises and firms invest more' with 'raises consumer spending (C) and investment (I)' - hasUnhandledLetterReference true, shuffleOptions returns the identical object. NEW FOOLING CASES AGAINST THE KEYWORD PATH, which is now the only path that rewrites anything - six constructed, six rewrite, none declines. The list continues over separators, joiners and bracketed glosses, so any standalone A-F reached that way is remapped whatever it means: 'Option C, B to D on the diagram, shows the fall in real output.' -> B (a diagram point) becomes C while D does not move; 'The answer C + I + G + (X-M) is the expenditure definition of aggregate demand.' -> the Consumption symbol becomes D, the exact corruption class the bare-bracket rule was deleted to prevent, now reachable through the keyword instead; 'the options B2B, B2C and C2C' -> 'C2B, B2C and C2C' (the letter is not standalone to a human but the tokeniser splits on the digit); 'Options A (a tax rise) and B (a spending cut), C and I are left unchanged.' -> C wrongly moved; 'The options (fiscal, monetary and supply-side) A government may use' -> A moved, because a gloss immediately after the keyword also opens the list; 'Statement A and B, D on the data-response paper' -> D moved. ZERO live instances: of the 262 remapped letters, 31 are reached by list continuation rather than sitting straight after the keyword, and I read all 31 - every one is a genuine 'Options A, C and D' reference. So this is one content edit away, exactly as the bracket rule was, but it is not shipping a defect today. STILL REMAINS, content work the fix itself marks Separately: pick-the-longest scores 70.2% (540/769) because option TEXT is untouched. THE 25 DECLINES, judged: all 25 are forced for the code as it stands, because a bracketed A-F cannot be told from a symbol either way without reading the sentence, and guessing wrong in either direction corrupts. But only 10 are unavoidable in content terms - aggregate-demand q1/q11/q13/q20, macroeconomic-objectives-policies q4/q11/q18, national-income q5/q13 and poverty-inequality q3, where the bracketed letter is the standard IAL expenditure identity C+I+G+(X-M) or the Gini A/(A+B) and cannot be edited away. The other 15 are recoverable: 14 are genuine option references written as bare '(A)' ('TV ads (A), billboards (B)') which shuffle immediately once rewritten as 'Option A' - verified by editing one and re-running - and marketing-mix-strategy q4 is the idiom 'from A to B'. So 10 unavoidable, 15 a judgement call about content effort.

code.title: Any key whose name starts with a-d (Ctrl, Alt, Arrow keys, Backspace, CapsLock) selects an answer
code.fix: Require `e.key.length === 1` before the letter comparison (and ignore events with ctrlKey/metaKey/altKey).
code.impact: A student who presses Ctrl (e.g. Ctrl+Tab to switch tab) or an arrow key to scroll has an answer silently selected and the card moves to phase 1 ('Check answer' lit). If they then press Enter expecting to advance, the wrong answer is checked and recorded into SM-2.

code.title: Confidence is never collected in Smart Practice; Learn Mode's confidence prompt writes to a localStorage key nothing reads
code.fix: Either add a 3-button confidence row to QuestionCard after reveal and pass it to computeNextReview (the lib already supports it), or remove the InlineQuiz confidence prompt until it feeds scheduling. Do not ship a prompt whose data is discarded.
code.impact: Lucky guesses in Smart Practice are scheduled identically to confident knowledge, so a B-guesser (see the bias finding) accumulates 'mastered' (repetitions>=3) cards they cannot actually answer. In Learn Mode the student is interrupted by a 4-second confidence prompt whose answer changes nothing they will ever see, which reads as a pointless widget.

code.title: 'This question will come back' is false within a session; 'RETRIED' stat counts questions that were never retried
code.fix: Re-append wrong items to the end of the in-session queue (cap once per item), or change the copy to 'Scheduled for review in 10 minutes' and rename the summary stat to 'To review'.
code.impact: A student who gets 6 wrong is told six times the question will come back, finishes the 20-question session without seeing any of them again, and then sees 'RETRIED 6' on the summary. The product promises a Leitner-style loop it does not deliver in the moment the student expects it.

code.title: Pre-test questions reappear as the block's inline quiz (~50% of sections) and the post-test is the identical 3 questions in identical order
code.fix: Exclude the union of all blocks' quizIndices from the pre-test pool; for the post-test, sample 3 DIFFERENT questions on the same sub-topics (or at least re-shuffle options) and label it honestly. Also fix the pre-test copy: 'Perfect — your brain is now primed' after 0/3 (PreTest.jsx:135) reads as sarcasm to a nervous student.
code.impact: Half of students see a pre-test question again a few minutes later as the 'Quick quiz' with the answer already revealed, and every student takes a post-test where remembering 'it was B' counts as improvement. The pre/post delta shown on the completion screen is not evidence of learning.
code.evidence: RE-CONFIRMED after the derangement retry landed. PostTest.jsx:65-70 tries salts 'post-test', 'post-test1' ... 'post-test7' until the option order actually differs from the pre-test's. Measured over the whole corpus by replaying what the pre-test stores (shuffleOptions(q,'') - the order StudyApp.jsx:388 hands to PreTest) and then running PostTest's exact loop: 769 questions, 744 shuffled, IDENTICAL REPLAYS 0, down from the 36 I measured before. Max salts used 3; the loop never exhausted its 8. Terminates for a declined question: shuffleOptions returns the same object identity when it declines, PostTest.jsx:68 breaks on 'moved === q', and decline does not depend on the salt, so all 25 declines exit on attempt 1 and are left alone on purpose. Carried userAnswer still points at the same option text: checked every possible pre-test choice on every shuffled question (744 x 4 = 2976 cases) through PostTest.jsx:71-74 - 0 cases where moved.options[at] is not the identical string the student picked. Out-of-range or non-numeric userAnswer falls back to the stored value (indexOf -1 path), so no silent reinterpretation. Two-option question still behaves: synthetic 2-option post-test ran on attempt 1, orders differ, correctIndex moved 1->0 and the correct option TEXT is preserved. RESIDUAL, not live and not blocking: for a 2-option question each salt has a 1/2 chance of the identity order, so the 8-salt loop can exhaust - a synthetic sweep of 744 two-option questions gave 4 identical replays (0.54%, against the 1/256 the loop predicts), and on exhaustion the loop keeps the last attempt, which is a valid question object with a correctly remapped explanation, just the same order. The live corpus has no such question: all 769 have exactly 4 options. The other half of the finding is unchanged from the previous confirmation - PostTest.jsx and PreTest.jsx are the only files in F079's scope touched since it, and the fallback post-test path (PostTest.jsx:34-40) and the pre-test's reserved-question exclusion (PreTest.jsx:17-28) are untouched by 6ce44e1.

Enforced at scripts/_content-write.mjs:102-107 and scripts/publish-section.mjs:114-124. code.title: React hydration fails on page load: script tags rendered inside React components make the server and client HTML disagree

Found live on /?section=supply during packet 9 verification; it predates packet 9 and is unrelated to it.

Remove first-letter hints from all six fillins (or make them optional after a wrong attempt) and replace the two non-causal reorders (PED goods ranking; recession/YED parallel outcomes) with classify/sort or numeric fillin exercises; move the extras chains/evaluation (all 1.1 market research content) to meeting-customer-needs and write on-topic ones (e.g. 'Cost-push shock -> supply shifts left -> price up, quantity down -> firms with inelastic demand pass costs on').

Supply and Factors Affecting Supply > what-is-supply > realExample (UK strawberry farmers): Backwards and teaches the wrong concept. UK strawberry retail prices are LOWEST in summer because that is peak season; farmers supply more in summer because of growing conditions (seasonality = a supply SHIFT), not because 'retail prices are highest'. Presented as 'the law of supply in action' (movement along the curve), it is a textbook example of the opposite. Also UK-centric for an international cohort.

content.text: Price Elasticity of Demand (PED) > ped-and-revenue > realExample (UK government tobacco taxation): Claims 'total tax revenue increases each year'. HMRC tobacco duty receipts peaked around 2021-22 (~£10.3bn) and have fallen since (~£8.8bn 2023-24, lower again 2024-25). Also conflates government tax revenue with a firm's total revenue (TR = P x Q), which is the concept being taught; the addictive-good framing is Economics 2.x/market failure territory.

Demand and Factors Affecting Demand > what-is-demand > realExample (Sony PS5): 'Sony cut the price of the PS5 in several markets to boost sales in 2024. As the price dropped, quantity demanded rose sharply.' Sony's headline 2024 move was a ~19% price RISE in Japan (Sept 2024), followed by rises in Europe/UK/Australia (Apr 2025) and the US (Aug 2025); 2024 saw only short promotional discounts, and PS5 shipments fell year-on-year in FY2024. The example as written is not true and will confuse students who read the news.

q18: Internally inconsistent and the explanation is unfinished. Revenue is exactly unchanged (500x$40 = $20,000; 400x$50 = $20,000), yet the keyed answer [0] says 'demand is inelastic so revenue rises'. The explanation literally contains 'Revenue rises from $20,000 to $20,000... actually revenue = ... However…' — a visible authoring note. A numerate student who checks the arithmetic will (correctly) reject the keyed answer.

content.text: Movement terminology: Edexcel mark schemes accept 'extension/contraction' — used in common_mistakes and flashcards but never taught in content (unsure whether the IAL scheme requires it; the GCE scheme does credit it).

Fix content[].quizIndices and practiceIndices so each block's inline quiz/practice tests what that block taught (currently 5 of 6 blocks show a mismatched MCQ, two of them on untaught material; the Promotion block's practice is an untaught USP question). Suggested mapping is in structureIssues[0]/[1].

Rewrite all 9 fill-in recalls: remove letter-pattern hints ('SM___', 'lo_', 'ty__'), stop putting the answer in an adjacent template line, and replace at least the Boston Matrix, design mix, promotion and distribution fillins with classification/placement exercises (quadrant drag, ATL/BTL sort, build-the-channel). Fix the two weak reorders (B2B stages, e-commerce transformation) per recallAudit.
Add diagrams: PLC sales+profit curve with extension-strategy bump, Boston Matrix 2x2 with cash-flow arrows, and a distribution-channel ladder; wire them via diagramRef on blocks 0 and 5.

Correct practice command words to IAL Business conventions (Define = 2, Explain = 4, Analyse = 6, Assess = 10/12, Evaluate = 20) and rewrite P2/P3 guidance as levels descriptors (KAA + evaluation with contextual judgement) instead of point-per-mark; add a short stimulus to the 10/20-markers.

Close the spec gaps with four short subsections: types of branding + ways to build a brand (incl. USP, sponsorship, emotional branding); design-mix social trends (resource depletion, waste minimisation, re-use/recycling); pricing social trends (online sales, price-comparison sites) and the spec's six pricing factors; mass vs niche marketing strategy and product-to-service distribution shift. Rename the section '1.3 Marketing mix and strategy' or split to match 1.3.1-1.3.5.

Distribution (Place) > changes-in-distribution > realExample (Warby Parker): Claims Warby Parker grew 'to a $3 billion valuation through direct distribution alone'. Warby Parker opened its first physical store in 2013 and now operates 200+ stores; its IPO valuation (2021) was ~$6bn and it is a multi-channel retailer. 'Direct distribution alone' is false and the number is unmoored from a date.

Pricing Strategies > factors-determining-pricing > body + recall: The factor list (costs, objectives, brand positioning, competition, PED, economy, legal) does not match the IAL spec list for 'factors that determine the most appropriate pricing strategy': number of USPs/amount of differentiation, PED, amount of competition, strength of brand, stage in the PLC, costs and need for profit. USPs/differentiation and PLC stage are missing; 'state of the economy' is not on the spec. A student revising to this list would miss two mark-scheme-listed factors.

q17: Same untaught intensive/selective/exclusive taxonomy as Q14. Additionally, 'own stores + website' is arguably 'direct distribution' (taught) rather than 'exclusive distribution' (untaught); a student who learned the section would pick the taught concept and be marked wrong. Distractor 3 does not offer 'direct'.

p0: 'Define the term USP (4 marks)'. In IAL Business (WBS11) 'Define' is a 2-mark command; the 4-mark command is 'Explain'. The model answer pads a definition with an example and a benefit to reach 4 points, which is not how a define question is marked. USP is also never taught in content[] yet this is the inline practice for block 3.

p1: 'Explain how a business might use extension strategies... (6 marks)'. IAL Business 'Explain' is 4 marks; 6 marks is 'Analyse'. Model answer gives 6 point-marks including a definition mark, which mismatches IAL's KAA levels for 6-markers. Also via practiceIndices=[1] on block 4 this PLC question is served at the end of the Pricing block, three blocks after PLC was taught.

Inline quiz mapping is off by one relative to teaching (content[].quizIndices = [0],[1],[2],[3],[4],[5] look auto-assigned sequentially, and LearnModeTab.jsx:106-108 indexes them straight into quiz[]): block 1 (Marketing Mix/Loyalty) shows the Boston Matrix Q1; block 2 (Design) shows the penetration-pricing Q2 BEFORE pricing is taught in block 4; block 3 (Promotion) shows the design-mix Q3; block 4 (Pricing) shows the distribution-channel Q4 BEFORE distribution is taught in block 5; block 5 (Distribution) shows the BTL Q5. Only block 0 is correct. Fix: block0 [0,1,11,10,6,16,18,20], block1 [9,19], block2 [3], block3 [5,13,22,24], block4 [2,8,12,15,21], block5 [4,7,14,17,23].

Inline practice mapping is wrong: practiceIndices [0] on block 3 and [1] on block 4 index into practice sorted by marks ascending (LearnModeTab.jsx:82,110-113), giving the Promotion block a USP 'Define' (untaught) and the Pricing block an extension-strategies question. P2 (pricing, 10 marks) is the obvious fit for block 4 and P4 (Boston) for block 0; P3 (integrated mix, 20 marks) for block 1. Three of five practice questions are never surfaced inline.

diagrams[] is empty (meta.diagrams = 0). The PLC sales/profit curve and the Boston Matrix 2x2 are the two models in this section that IAL papers expect students to sketch or read; teaching them as bullet lists only is the single biggest pedagogical gap. A distribution-channel ladder diagram would also help block 5.

Section is numbered '1.3.3' but its scope is the whole IAL topic 1.3 (1.3.1 Product/service design, 1.3.2 Branding and promotion, 1.3.3 Pricing strategies, 1.3.4 Distribution, 1.3.5 Marketing strategy). In the spec, 1.3.3 is 'Pricing strategies' alone. Students cross-referencing the spec or past-paper labels will be confused. Either rename to '1.3 Marketing mix and strategy' or split into five sections matching the spec.

Block order does not follow the spec: block 0 is 1.3.5 (strategy: PLC, Boston) and block 1 mixes an untethered '4Ps' intro with 1.3.5 items (B2B/B2C, loyalty), then 1.3.1-1.3.4 follow. Better: 4Ps overview first, then design → promotion/branding → pricing → distribution → strategy (PLC/Boston/B2B/loyalty/mass-vs-niche), so that pricing and promotion can reference the PLC as prior knowledge and the strategy block can synthesise.

'Marketing Objectives' (SMART etc.) is not an IAL 1.3 spec item; it is a reasonable primer but occupies the first step of the section, which given the 75% step-0 abandonment rate is the most expensive real estate in the section. Consider moving it into the 4Ps step or cutting it.

2-per-step pairing produces two orphan single-section steps with heavy widget stacks: 'Boston Matrix' alone (with quiz + takeaway + spaced recall from PLC + its own immediate fillin) and 'Customer Loyalty' alone, 'Viral Marketing' alone. The branding reorder recall duplicates the branding flow block visible on the same step, so 'immediate' recall is copying.

Block 2 title 'Product/Service Design' covers only the design mix and ethical sourcing; the block's takeaway ('Social trends toward sustainability are reshaping product design') is not supported by content on waste minimisation / re-use / recycling / resource depletion, which the spec lists explicitly.

Block 3 takeaway 'ATL reaches mass audiences; BTL is targeted and measurable' is fine, but block 3 never teaches types of branding (individual/family/corporate) or ways to build a brand beyond 'consistent identity', so a student cannot answer the 'types of branding' knowledge questions IAL papers set. Takeaways otherwise match their blocks accurately.

Misconceptions are genuinely good: all 15 describe real student errors (vague objectives, rigid PLC, always-divest Dogs, 4Ps in isolation, points = loyalty, design-mix as separate decisions, ethical = less profit, advertising is best, brand = logo, virality on demand, penetration for everything, cost-only pricing, direct is best, e-commerce kills retail). Not filler.

Difficulty ramp is flat: every section follows the identical template (definition paragraph → flow → paragraph → example), analysis/evaluation lives only in examMatters text, and the only evaluation exercises are the three 'pick the hedged option' MCQs. No section escalates to an applied mini-case.
1.3.2 Types of branding: individual brand, brand family (family branding), corporate/own brand — not taught anywhere in content[].
1.3.2 Ways to build a brand: USPs/differentiation, advertising, sponsorship, use of social media — USP and sponsorship absent from content (USP appears only in quiz Q13 and practice P0).
1.3.2 Changes in branding and promotion to reflect social trends: 'emotional branding' is named in the spec and only appears in the B2B section as a contrast; not taught as a concept.
1.3.2 Types of promotion: public relations and sponsorship omitted from the ATL/BTL list.

1.3.1 Changes in the elements of the design mix to reflect social trends: concern over resource depletion, designing for waste minimisation, re-use and recycling — only 'ethical sourcing' is covered; the circular-design bullets are missing.

1.3.3 Factors that determine the most appropriate pricing strategy: 'number of USPs / amount of differentiation' and 'stage in the product life cycle' are not in the factors section (PLC is mentioned once in passing in the methods intro).

1.3.3 Changes in pricing to reflect social trends: online sales and price comparison sites — not taught (EasyJet dynamic pricing example gestures at online pricing but price-comparison sites are absent).
1.3.4 Changes to distribution to reflect social trends: 'changing from product to service' (e.g. streaming replacing physical media, subscription models) — not taught.
1.3.5 Marketing strategies appropriate for different types of market: mass markets vs niche markets — not taught as a topic ('niche' appears only inside two misconceptions).
1.3.5 Consumer behaviour: how businesses develop customer loyalty — covered; but the spec framing 'consumer behaviour' (e.g. rational vs emotional decision-making) is only touched via B2B/B2C.

Unsure: whether the current IAL spec wording for distribution channels uses the '4-stage / 2-stage / direct' terminology; content uses 'zero-level / one-level / two-level', which is fine conceptually but may not match mark-scheme vocabulary.

Re-map quizIndices/practiceIndices so each block's inline MCQ and practice question is on-topic (Planning->Q12/Q19 + practice 3; Internal->Q0/Q16 + practice 2; External->Q2/Q14 + practice 1/4; Forms->Q4; Liability->Q1/Q23) and drop 'Define cash flow' until cash flow is taught.

Add the missing spec content: a subsection on cash-flow forecasts (simple table, interpretation, uses and limitations) and a subsection on the remaining external sources/methods (family and friends, business angels, peer-to-peer, leasing, trade credit, grants), and rewrite 'choosing-appropriate-finance' to actually cover finance appropriate to limited vs unlimited liability businesses.

Remove first-three-letter hints from all six fill-ins (or replace them with scenario/numeric fill-ins), and replace the 'Match the finance source' reorder with a real matching widget or fill-in; strip bracketed durations from the shortest-to-longest reorder.

Fix factual/UK-centric content: replace the Tesla and JCB examples, correct the Raspberry Pi dilution claim, resolve the 'retained profit has no cost' vs opportunity-cost contradiction, and swap HMRC/Companies House/'per pound' for international wording; add at least two Asia/Middle East examples.

Normalise practice to IAL formats (Define 2 marks, Explain 4 marks, drop 'Outline', add a short case context to the Assess/Evaluate questions and levels-based guidance) and cut the out-of-scope/joke MCQs (Q5, Q8, Q6, Q9, duplicate Q10) in favour of items on cash-flow forecasts and finance-by-liability-type.

Liability and Appropriate Finance > choosing-appropriate-finance > realExample (Tesla): States Tesla funded gigafactory construction with 'government loans' and 'retained profits' and that Musk 'matched each source to its purpose'. Tesla's US DOE loan ($465m, 2010, repaid 2013) funded the Fremont plant, not the Gigafactory; Gigafactory Nevada (2014-16) was funded by equity/convertible notes, Panasonic and state tax abatements; Tesla had no retained profits (cumulative losses until 2020). The narrative is invented.
q5: Franchising is not taught anywhere in this section (it is a Unit 1 'forms of business' point). Option 'Unlimited liability protection' is a nonsense phrase, not a plausible distractor.
q8: Social enterprise is not taught in this section (Unit 1 content). Explanation is fine but the item is out of scope for a section quiz/pre-test.

p0: 'Define the term cash flow (4 marks)' — IAL Business 'Define' questions are 2 marks; and cash flow / cash-flow forecasts are not taught anywhere in this section's content, yet this is the inline practice for block 3 'External Sources of Finance'. Guidance awards marks for inflow/outflow examples and positive/negative cash flow, which is not a definition mark scheme.

quizIndices are simply 0,1,2,3,4 in block order, not topic-matched: block 1 (Planning) shows Q0 internal finance; block 2 (Internal) shows Q1 unlimited liability; block 4 (Forms of business) shows Q3 overdraft. Only blocks 3 and 5 get an on-topic inline MCQ. Fix by mapping e.g. Planning->Q12/Q19, Internal->Q0/Q16, External->Q2/Q14, Forms->Q4, Liability->Q1/Q23.

practiceIndices are likewise misaligned: block 3 (External) gets practice 0 'Define cash flow' (untaught term); block 4 (Forms of Business) gets practice 1 on venture capital. Practice 2, 3, 4 (the three best questions) are never surfaced in Learn Mode.

Block order teaches share capital / Ltd vs PLC (block 3, share-capital) before Ltd, PLC and limited liability are defined (blocks 4-5). Forms of business and liability should precede external finance, or at minimum precede the share-capital subsection.

Block 5 'Liability and Appropriate Finance' is largely a restatement: unlimited-vs-limited-liability repeats what sole-traders-partnerships and private-public-limited-companies already said, while the spec's actual bullet (which finance sources are available to unlimited- vs limited-liability businesses, e.g. only companies can issue shares; sole traders rely on owner's capital, loans, overdrafts, personal guarantees) is never made.

Within block 2 the 2-per-step pairing yields (retained profit + sale of assets) then owner's capital alone; the spec and start-up logic put owner's capital first, so the lone third step is the one that should open the block.

Several 'flow' widgets are not flows: sole-traders-partnerships 'Simple to set up -> Owner keeps all profit -> Unlimited personal liability' is a feature list; unlimited-vs-limited-liability 'Business fails -> Unlimited: assets seized -> Limited: only share value lost' presents a branch as a linear chain.

Misconceptions are mostly genuine student errors (good), except contents-of-business-plans ('students list every section without explaining') which is an exam-technique tip, not a misconception; examMatters already covers it.
Takeaways match their blocks. Block 1 takeaway 'Financial forecasts are the most scrutinised section by lenders' is presented as fact from a hedged body claim ('often').

Real examples are 10/12 UK companies (Deliveroo, Grind, Aldi UK, BA, JCB, Raspberry Pi, BrewDog, Pimlico Plumbers, ASOS, BHS) for an international audience; only Spanx and Tesla are non-UK and Tesla is wrong. No Asian/Middle Eastern examples.
Zero diagrams; a debt-vs-equity comparison table and a simple cash-flow forecast table (a spec requirement) would be the obvious visual anchors for this section.

No difficulty ramp: every subsection follows the identical template (paragraph, flow, paragraph, paragraph) with recall difficulty flat across the section; the 20-mark evaluation skills (weighing factors against a context) are only exercised in practice questions the flow never shows.

Inventory Management > just-in-time > realExample: Claims Toyota 'had to halt production at 14 factories because its JIT system had no buffer stock of chips' in the 2021 semiconductor shortage. This inverts the well-documented story: after the 2011 Fukushima earthquake Toyota deliberately built a business-continuity plan holding 2-6 months of chip stock, and in early 2021 it was widely reported as the carmaker LEAST affected by the chip shortage precisely because it broke from pure JIT for semiconductors. The August/September 2021 cuts at 14 plants were driven mainly by COVID outbreaks at parts suppliers in Malaysia/Vietnam. A student who repeats this line to an examiner who knows the case loses credibility.

Recall design: 5/5 fillins have letter-leaking hints plus templates that paraphrase the body; 6/7 reorders impose order on parallel concepts; all 12 exercises are copies of body flows/bullets rather than transfer tasks; only two shuffle permutations are used across 7 reorders ([2,0,3,1] x3, [3,1,0,2] x3), making the pattern learnable. Three hints have length mismatches vs the answer ('in___________' 13 vs 'independence' 12; 'sa___________' 13 vs 'satisfaction' 12; 'fi________' 10 vs 'financial' 9).

Filler misconceptions: 'the biggest barrier is lack of a good idea' (barriers), 'the best decision is one with no trade-offs' (trade-offs), 'a good manager can achieve all objectives at once' (conflicts) are not things IAL students actually write. The genuine ones are: 'anyone who runs a business is an entrepreneur', 'born not made', 'opportunity cost = money spent', 'all businesses aim to maximise profit', 'social enterprises are charities'.

examMatters is repetitive: 7 of 12 end with a variant of 'always link to the case study context'; none explains the IAL level-mark structure (K/A/An/E) or the 'however/depends on' evaluation moves that WBS11 mark schemes reward.

Duplicate flashcards: the two 'chain' cards ('Trace the chain from an entrepreneur identifying an opportunity...' and 'Trace the impact of different leadership styles...') each appear twice (22 cards, 20 unique fronts).

Notes[] and extras[] cover things content[] does not (profit satisficing, limited liability, sole trader/partnership/Ltd/PLC chain, government support, hard vs soft skills) — students in Learn Mode never see them, while the quiz bank assumes them.

Difficulty ramp and block order are sensible (role -> motives -> objectives -> choices, matching 1.5.1 -> 1.5.2 -> 1.5.3 -> 1.5.5); takeaways match their blocks apart from the 'barriers to entry' wording in Block 0. Zero diagrams is acceptable for this topic but a one-glance 'objective vs life-cycle stage' or 'opportunity cost = next best, not sum' visual would replace the passive fillins.

content.text: Unsure: whether the current WBS11 papers use 'Define' (4 marks) or only 'Explain one' (4 marks) — practice Q0 tariff should be checked against a recent past paper.

Rebuild the practice set for WBS12 scope and IAL tariffs: delete the gearing (idx 1) and ROCE/asset-turnover/dividend-yield (idx 3) questions; add a 4-mark 'Calculate the current ratio and acid test ratio' from a mini statement of financial position, a 4-mark 'Explain one way...', a 10/12-mark 'Assess the internal causes of X's failure', and a 20-mark 'Evaluate whether improving liquidity or profitability should be the priority'; write levels-based guidance that explicitly requires a judgement (remove 'No explicit judgement mark').

Fix the recall layer: remove 3-letter prefix hints on all 7 fill-ins (use word banks with distractors or numeric blanks); delete the duplicate income-statement reorder in net-profit and replace with a numeric profit-ladder fill-in; replace the external-causes 'gradual to sudden' reorder with a causal chain (recession -> income falls -> demand falls -> revenue below fixed costs -> cash exhausted -> closure) or an internal/external sort.

Add the missing spec content as sections: statement of financial position (with a labelled mini example students can extract current assets/liabilities from), working capital and its management, operating profit margin, and a short profit-vs-cash section; introduce the IAL terms 'statement of comprehensive income' and 'profit for the year'; fix the 'Net profit (also called operating profit...)' sentence.

Repair the quiz: reword Q15 to ask for operating profit (or supply interest and tax), rewrite Q19's explanation so it does not claim raising current liabilities improves working capital, dedupe Q5/Q17 and Q9/Q13, replace the three 'Evaluate...' length-giveaway MCQs with content questions on the balance sheet and improving profitability, and remap block 4 quizIndices from [3] to a business-failure item (Q6) and block 3 practiceIndices away from the gearing question.

Correct the Carillion example (it was loss-making, not 'profitable on paper', at collapse), reconcile the 'selling assets' contradiction in the Liquidity block, and add two diagrams (profit waterfall; working capital cycle) since the section currently has none.

Understanding Profit > net-profit > body[0]: 'Net profit (also called operating profit or profit for the year, depending on the level of deduction)' conflates operating profit with net profit. IAL distinguishes operating profit (before interest and tax) from profit for the year (net profit). The section's own flow then says net = after interest and tax, quiz Q0 correctly calls revenue - COS - opex 'operating profit', and Q15 calls the same computation 'net profit'. Three inconsistent messages.

q15: No interest or tax given, so $80,000 is OPERATING profit, not net profit / profit for the year. Q0 labels the identical computation 'operating profit', and the section itself defines net profit as after interest and tax. Directly contradicts the content it tests.

p3: 'Evaluate which financial ratios would be most useful for an investor... (20 marks)' — tariff matches IAL Evaluate, but the model answer is built on ROCE, gearing, asset turnover and dividend yield. Gearing and ROCE are Unit 3 (WBS13 ratio analysis); asset turnover and dividend yield are not on the IAL Business spec at all. None are taught in this section. Guidance is point-allocated (2+3+3+2+2+2+2+2+2) rather than the levels-based scheme IAL uses for 20-markers.

content.text: p2: 'Assess the importance of liquidity management for a rapidly growing small business. (10 marks)' — tariff correct. But guidance is point-based and states 'No explicit judgement mark' — wrong for IAL: Assess is levels-marked and Level 4 requires a supported judgement/conclusion. Guidance actively steers students away from the thing that earns top level.

Meta number '2.3.3' with title 'Managing Finance' does not match the IAL spec structure: 2.3 is 'Managing finance' with 2.3.1 Profit, 2.3.2 Liquidity, 2.3.3 Business failure. This section bundles all of 2.3 (unsure of exact sub-numbering, confident of the structure).

Duplicate recall on consecutive steps: net-profit's reorder (shown 'spaced' at top of step B) and structure-of-income-statement's reorder (shown 'immediate' at bottom of step C) are the same four income-statement lines.

Blocks 1 ('Understanding Profit') and 2 ('Income Statement') overlap heavily: net-profit already walks the statement top-to-bottom, so block 2 section 1 re-teaches it. Better split: Block 1 = profit calculations + statement of comprehensive income; Block 2 = profitability ratios + improving profitability.

Inline quiz mapping is wrong for block 4: quizIndices [3] shows the acid-test MCQ at the end of 'Causes of Business Failure'. Inline practice mapping is wrong for block 3: practiceIndices [1] shows the gearing question (untaught) at the end of 'Liquidity'. Blocks 1 and 4 have no practice at all, so practice 2 (liquidity Assess) and 4 (improve NPM) are never surfaced in Learn Mode.

No practice question on business failure, the block with the most evaluative potential (typical IAL: 'Assess the likely causes of X's failure' 10/12 marks), and no 'Calculate' question even though IAL Unit 2 routinely asks 4-mark calculate current ratio / acid test / margin from a table.

Zero diagrams for a section that is naturally visual: a revenue -> gross profit -> operating profit -> profit for the year waterfall, and a working capital cycle. Flashcards already contain a working-capital-cycle 'Trace' chain that has no counterpart in content[].

Flashcards and quiz test content not in content[]: statement of financial position, current assets/liabilities definitions, working capital. Learners hit these in free Notes/Flashcards or quiz without ever having been taught them in Learn Mode.
Flashcards 19-21 are exact duplicates of 22-24 (three 'Trace...' cards repeated).
Takeaway for Liquidity block contradicts its own body (sale of underused assets listed as an option in body, forbidden in takeaway/misconception).

Step pairing (gross+net, improve alone; structure+interpreting; understanding+ratios, improving alone; internal+external, why-new alone) is coherent. Difficulty ramp (calculations -> statement -> liquidity -> failure) is sensible.

Misconceptions are mostly real student errors (gross vs net; higher revenue = higher profit; income statement as snapshot; profit = cash; 2:1 rule; bottom-line only). 'Students assume having a good idea is enough' (why-new-businesses) is filler, not an exam misconception.
All seven fill-ins share one design flaw: hints are the first three letters of the answer, so the recall widget tests spelling completion rather than understanding. Systemic, not per-item.
2.3.1 Profit: operating profit margin — not taught as a section (only named in an extras chain); only GPM and NPM are taught.
2.3.1 Profit: 'statement of comprehensive income' and 'profit for the year' — the IAL labels students will see on data tables are never introduced.
2.3.1 Profit: distinction between profit and cash — only covered obliquely inside the Liquidity block; no dedicated treatment (e.g. credit sales, depreciation, capital purchases, loan repayments).
2.3.2 Liquidity: statement of financial position (balance sheet) — not taught at all in content[]; only appears in flashcards and one misconception aside.
2.3.2 Liquidity: working capital and its management / the importance of cash — not taught in content[] despite being quizzed (Q9, Q13, Q19) and flashcarded.
2.3.3 Business failure: internal causes list is reasonable; spec examples such as marketing failure and poor quality are only in flashcards, not content (minor).

Unsure: whether the IAL spec expects calculation of the current/acid test ratios from a supplied statement of financial position — content teaches the formulas but never shows a statement to extract figures from.

Fix the two broken inline quizzes: replace the duplicate '£500' option in quiz[3] (e.g. with -£500 and £3,500) and change content[1].quizIndices from [1] to [8] so the Sales Forecasting block asks a forecasting question.

Add a labelled break-even chart diagram (FC, TC, TR lines; BEP; profit/loss zones; margin of safety) with diagramRef on the Break-Even block, and a cash-flow table diagram for block 3; without them the 'Break-Even Charts' subsection and its reorder are teaching a picture nobody sees.

Rewrite practice[] to IAL shape: a 4-mark 'Calculate' (break-even + margin of safety from given figures), a 2-mark 'What is meant by', a case-anchored 4-mark 'Explain one', a 10-mark 'Assess' and a 20-mark 'Evaluate' with short stimulus extracts, and replace additive points-marking with levels descriptors (K/A/An/E). Wire practiceIndices onto blocks 0, 1 and 4.
Add the missing spec content to block 4: historical vs zero-based budgets and difficulties of budgeting (currently only in quiz Q6/flashcards), and add total contribution to block 2.

Replace the two non-genuine reorders (fixed-vs-variable ranking; predictability ranking) with classification/matching exercises, and convert the five trivial collocation fillins (revenue, forecasting, cash-basics, improving-cash-flow, budgets) into numeric or spec-term fillins; regenerate distinct shuffle permutations per recall.

q3: Options [0] and [2] are both '£500'. Two identical options, only index 0 marked correct — a student picking [2] is marked wrong for the right answer. This is the inline MCQ for the Cash-Flow block (quizIndices [3]), so every Learn Mode user hits it.

content.text: q1: Wired as the inline quiz for the 'Sales Forecasting' block (content[1].quizIndices = [1]) before break-even has been taught (block 2). The block has an on-topic question available (Q8, new business with no historical data) that is not used.

q20: Evaluation-as-MCQ: the correct option is the only long, hedged, two-sided one; distractors ('always perfectly accurate', 'useless', 'only manufacturing') are absurd. Answerable by length cue with no knowledge. Same pattern in Q21, Q22, Q24.
q24: Distractors 'They are illegal for businesses to use' and 'They only cover a single day' are not plausible to anyone; question tests nothing.

p0: 'Define the term break-even output (4 marks)'. IAL Business definition questions ('What is meant by...'/'Define') are 2 marks. The 4x1 mark guidance (definition, zero profit, formula, profit/loss zones) is not how a definition is marked; a student trained on this will over-write 2-markers.

p2: 'Assess ... (10 marks)' is a valid IAL allocation, but the guidance is additive points-marking ('2 marks', '1 mark' per point, summing to 10). IAL Business 8/10/12-mark Assess questions are levels-marked (Level 1-4 across Knowledge, Application, Analysis, Evaluation). Also no case-study stimulus is provided for the 'growing restaurant chain', so the Application strand cannot be demonstrated.

p3: 'Evaluate ... (20 marks)' — the 20-mark allocation exists in IAL Business, but the guidance again sums 2-mark points to 20 rather than describing the L1-L4 KAAE levels and the need for a justified judgement. Question is context-free ('business decision-making'); IAL 20-markers are always anchored to the case extract.

p-1: No 'Calculate' question at all (break-even, margin of safety, total contribution, closing balance, variance) despite 4-mark Calculate questions appearing on almost every WBS12 paper. Only 2 of the 5 questions are wired into Learn Mode (practiceIndices on blocks 2 and 3); blocks 0, 1 and 4 get no inline practice even though the budgets question (index 2) and cash-flow question (index 4) exist.

Zero diagrams (content[].diagramRef all null, diagrams = 0) in a section containing a whole subsection 'Break-Even Charts' that describes three lines and an intersection verbally, a reorder recall 'Order the steps to draw a break-even chart', and an examMatters demanding 'precise drawing'. The IAL spec bullet is 'interpretation of break-even charts' — impossible to practise without one. A second diagram (cash-flow table with opening/closing balances) would serve 'cash-flow-forecasts'.

Block 1 'Sales Forecasting' inline MCQ is quizIndices [1] = break-even calculation (LearnModeTab.jsx:106-108 picks it directly). Block 3 'Cash-Flow Forecasting' inline MCQ (quizIndices [3]) has duplicate options. So 2 of the 5 inline quizzes a Learn Mode user sees are broken.

2-per-step pairing: blocks 0, 2, 3 have 3 sections so their second step carries one section plus all block-end widgets (InlineQuiz, InlinePractice, ExplainItBack, Takeaway); blocks 1 and 4 have 2 sections so the entire block, including both NoteSections and all widgets, lands on a single step. Step weight swings from ~1 section to 2 sections + 5 widgets.

Recall placement interacts badly with this section's authoring pattern (every first section has a fillin, every second section has a reorder). Per LearnModeTab.jsx:345-350 and :397-403, the immediate slot always shows currentRecalls[0] (so 8/8 fillins render as immediates, 0 reorders do) and the spaced slot shows the previous step's LAST section recall. Result: profit-and-loss, break-even-evaluation and improving-cash-flow fillins render twice back-to-back (bottom of one step, top of the next), the variance-analysis reorder (last section of last step) never renders, and the 4 other reorders only appear as 'spaced' recalls.

Only two shuffle patterns are used across all five reorders ([2,0,3,1] x3, [3,1,0,2] x2): a student who notices that the third-listed item always goes first can game them. Generate per-recall permutations.

Sequencing: cash-flow forecasting (block 3) is spec 2.3.1 'Planning' content and improving cash flow is 2.3.3 'Liquidity' content; neither neighbouring section covers them (planning-raising-finance has no cash-flow block; managing-finance has 'improving-liquidity'), so keeping them here is defensible but 'improving-cash-flow' now overlaps managing-finance > improving-liquidity. Cross-link rather than duplicate.

Takeaways match their blocks and are accurate; block 2 takeaway correctly restates BEP = FC / contribution. Misconceptions are real student errors (revenue = profit; TC line from origin; favourable = always good; borrow first) rather than filler — this is a strength. Difficulty ramp is sensible (definitions -> calculation -> evaluation) within blocks 2 and 3, but block 1 (forecasting) is entirely descriptive with no calculation or data, and block 4 ends the section on a definition-level note with no calculation practice for variances.
Block 0 realExample emoji for Ocado and Tesco are both the shopping-cart emoji; trivial but shows unreviewed generation.
2.3.2(d) Types of budget: historical figures vs zero-based budgeting — not in content[]; only appears in quiz Q6 and two flashcards.

2.3.2(d) Difficulties of budgeting — touched in one paragraph of purpose-of-budgets (restrictive, discourages initiative) but the standard mark-scheme points (based on forecasts that may be wrong, time-consuming to set, can cause budget-padding/use-it-or-lose-it behaviour, unrealistic targets demotivate) are only in extras.evaluation, not taught.
2.3.2(c) Total contribution (contribution per unit x units sold) and using it to calculate profit (total contribution - fixed costs) — only contribution per unit is taught; no total contribution.
2.3.2(b) Calculation of sales volume vs sales revenue as distinct quantities — 'sales volume' as a term is never used in content (it appears only in common_mistakes).
2.3.2(c) Interpretation of break-even charts — described verbally but with no chart to interpret; effect on BEP of a change in price/FC/VC (a standard IAL question) is not worked through.

2.3.2(a) Difficulties of sales forecasting as a discrete evaluative list (lack of data for new products, market volatility, bias of the forecaster, cost of research) — partially covered under 'accuracy depends on'; unsure whether IAL mark schemes require more than this.
Semi-variable costs and stepped fixed costs — mentioned only in extras.evaluation; unsure whether the IAL spec names semi-variable costs explicitly (Edexcel GCE does).

Add Learn-content blocks for the untaught spec bullets (strategy vs tactics + resource impact; PESTLE + Five Forces; portfolio analysis/BCG + distinctive capabilities), OR remove/quarantine quiz items 3,5,6,7,9 so the pre-test only samples taught material.
Add diagrams for Ansoff's matrix, Porter's strategic matrix (2x2) and the SWOT grid, ideally interactive 'drag this example into the right cell' rather than static images.

Rename 'Porter's Generic Strategies' to 'Porter's Strategic Matrix' and present four cells; fix the Ansoff takeaway to stop ranking product development below market development (and match notes[] which say both are medium risk).

Fix the Netflix SWOT example (password-sharing crackdown is an internal decision, not an external threat; debt weakness is dated) and the Amazon Ansoff example (AWS is diversification, not product development).

Replace the two untaught-topic practice questions with case-applied Ansoff and Porter questions (e.g. 8/10-mark 'Assess whether X should pursue market development or product development'), and attach level-descriptor mark schemes to the 10- and 20-markers.

Strategic Direction > porters-generic-strategies (title, keyIdea, body para 3, block takeaway 'Porter's three strategies'): IAL spec bullet and Edexcel mark schemes use 'Porter's Strategic Matrix' (a 2x2: cost leadership, differentiation, cost focus, differentiation focus). Content presents it as 'Porter's Generic Strategies' with 'three strategies'. Students may not recognise the exam wording, and 'choose one of three' misrepresents the four-cell matrix the spec names.

Corporate Objectives & Strategy > swot-analysis > realExample (Netflix): 'password-sharing crackdowns alienating users' is listed as an external THREAT, but the crackdown is Netflix's own 2023 policy decision (internal), and it in fact drove subscriber growth. Using it as a threat models the exact S/W vs O/T categorisation error the section is trying to teach. 'high debt from original content spend' as a weakness is also dated: Netflix has been strongly free-cash-flow positive since 2022.
q3: BCG/portfolio analysis is never taught in content[] (only in flashcards and notes). Pre-test and inline/post quiz draw from this bank, so students are tested on untaught material.

q5: Genuinely ambiguous: minimum wage is routinely classified as Political (government policy), Economic (labour cost) or Legal in Edexcel resources; the explanation itself concedes 'it could also have economic implications'. Two options are defensible. PESTLE is also not taught in content[].

Only 2 blocks x 2 sections = 2 Learn steps for a spec area (3.1.1-3.1.3) with ~10 bullets; each step is two long reading cards followed by one MCQ, one practice question and ExplainItBack. Very thin for the pre-test/post-test comparison to mean anything.

Quiz bank mismatch: 5 of 10 MCQs (indices 3,5,6,7,9) test BCG, PESTLE, Five Forces and strategic/tactical decisions, none of which appear in content[]. With PreTest sampling 3 random questions, most pre-tests will include at least one untaught item, which directly feeds the 'pre-test demotivates' complaint.

Block 1 is titled 'Corporate Objectives & Strategy' but never defines 'strategy' or 'tactics' (those definitions exist only in notes[]); the strategy-vs-tactics distinction is a named spec bullet and appears in quiz Q8.

Takeaways do match their blocks; misconceptions are genuine (not filler). The four misconceptions and examMatters are the strongest part of the section.

Practice questions and Learn content are disjoint on Ansoff/Porter: the two most examinable frameworks in the block have no applied practice question, while two practice questions (objective conflict, changing objectives) cover untaught ideas.

Notes[] hierarchy (mission → aims → corporate objectives → functional objectives) and flashcards disagree with content[] hierarchy (no 'aims'); cross-tab inconsistency will confuse students who move between Learn and Notes.

content.text: Unsure: whether the IAL spec expects Porter's matrix as four cells (cost focus / differentiation focus split) in mark schemes; content presents three strategies

Re-align assessment to teaching: either add a block 'Why grow, and what goes wrong' teaching internal/external economies of scale, diseconomies and overtrading (lift from extras.chains[2],[3] and flashcards), or pin quizIndices/practiceIndices per block so PreTest/InlineQuiz only draw from taught items. Right now half the quiz bank and 3/5 practice questions are untaught.

Replace the demergers subsection (off-spec, and its eBay/Skype example is factually wrong: it was a stake sale, not a demerger) with 'Problems of growth: diseconomies of scale and overtrading', which fixes both the spec gap and the incoherent block-2 pairing.

Add an InlineDiagram for block 1: supply chain (raw materials > manufacturer > distributor > retailer > consumer) with arrows showing backward vertical, forward vertical and horizontal integration, matching common_mistakes[1].

Add recall widgets: a fillin on the four integration types (e.g. 'A car maker buying a steel mill is ___ vertical integration; buying a dealership network is ___; buying a rival car maker is ___') and a reorder of the takeover-to-synergy sequence already given as a flow in external-growth-methods.

Swap practice idx 2 (Ansoff) and idx 3 (barriers to entry) for on-spec items, e.g. 'Explain one problem a business may face from rapid growth (4)' and 'Assess the financial risks and rewards to [case firm] of a takeover of [target] (10)', and add a levels-style mark scheme (KAA/Evaluation bands) to the 10- and 20-markers so students can self-mark; de-UK the CMA/MegaRetail references for the international audience.

Growth Decisions > demergers-splitting-up > realExample: States 'eBay demerged Skype in 2009, eventually selling it to Microsoft'. eBay did not demerge Skype (shareholders received no Skype shares); it sold a ~65-70% stake to a Silver Lake-led investor group in 2009, and that group sold Skype to Microsoft in 2011 for $8.5bn. This is a divestment/sale, which contradicts the section's own definition of a demerger two paragraphs earlier.

Growth Decisions > demergers-splitting-up (whole subsection incl. examMatters 'Examiners test whether you can evaluate demergers'): Demergers are an Edexcel Economics (WEC13 3.1.3) topic, not a WBS13 3.2 Business growth bullet. The examMatters claim that IAL Business examiners test demergers is, to my knowledge, unfounded and displaces spec content (diseconomies, overtrading, financial risks/rewards of takeovers) that IS examined.

content.text: q0: Correct answer (index 1) is right, but internal vs external economies of scale are never taught anywhere in content[] (only in flashcards/extras). Because PreTest draws 3 random MCQs and inline quizzes draw from this bank, students are gated/assessed on untaught material.

q2: Answer correct, but diseconomies of scale are only mentioned in passing (one clause in external-growth misconception and staying-small examMatters); never taught as a concept with causes. Untaught material in the assessment bank.
q3: Answer correct and well-explained, but overtrading does not appear anywhere in content[]. It is a named IAL spec bullet (problems arising from growth) so it should be taught, not just quizzed.

q7: Same as index 3: untaught. Also the explanation only justifies the correct answer and one distractor; 'Rapid recruitment of new staff' as a distractor is fine but should be explained as worsening cash outflow.

p2: 'Assess the usefulness of Ansoff's Matrix for a business deciding on its growth strategy' (10 marks) is a 3.1 Business objectives and strategy question, not 3.2 Business growth; Ansoff is never mentioned in this section's content. Also the question is generic ('a business') while a specific gym-chain context is supplied; IAL would phrase it 'Assess the usefulness of Ansoff's Matrix to the gym chain when deciding its growth strategy'. Mark allocation (10, Assess) is correct for IAL Business.

p3: 'Explain two barriers to entry that might prevent new firms from entering a market' (4 marks) is off-topic for 3.2 Business growth (it is Economics / at best 3.5 competitiveness). Nothing in content[] teaches barriers to entry. Should be replaced with an on-spec 4-marker (e.g. 'Explain one reason why a growing business might experience diseconomies of scale' or 'Explain one problem of rapid growth').

Assessment/teaching mismatch: 5 of 10 MCQs (idx 0,2,3,7,8) and 3 of 5 practice questions (idx 0,2,3) test economies of scale, diseconomies, overtrading, Ansoff and barriers to entry, none of which are taught in content[]. With quizIndices/practiceIndices null, the PreTest gate (3 random MCQs) and each block's InlineQuiz/InlinePractice can surface untaught questions, which directly feeds the founder's 'pre-test demotivates' hypothesis.

Zero recall widgets in either block: Learn Mode has no retrieval practice at all for this section. Obvious candidates: reorder 'takeover process' (identify target > bid premium > regulator review > integration > synergies realised/lost) from external-growth flow; fillin on the four integration types using the supermarket/food-processor/farm/delivery chain.

Zero diagrams: common_mistakes[1] literally tells students to 'draw a simple supply chain diagram in your head' (raw materials > manufacturing > distribution > retail > consumer) to place the two firms. That should be an actual InlineDiagram on block 1 (with backward/forward/horizontal arrows).

2-per-step pairing: with 2 sections per block the whole section is 2 steps. Block 1 pairing (organic + external) is coherent. Block 2 pairs 'Reasons for Staying Small' with 'Demergers', which are unrelated concepts; a student gets one step with two disconnected ideas. Replace demergers with 'Problems of growth: diseconomies and overtrading' so block 2 becomes 'When growth goes wrong / when not to grow'.

Difficulty ramp: the section jumps from definitional prose straight to a 20-mark evaluate with no intermediate teaching of the economic logic (why grow: economies of scale, market power; why it hurts: diseconomies, overtrading). The extras.chains[2] and [3] contain exactly this material, so it exists but is paywalled/hidden from the Learn Mode path.

Takeaways: Block 1 takeaway[3] ('culture clash is the primary reason') overclaims relative to the body. Block 2 takeaway[3] tells students to evaluate demergers from stakeholder perspectives, which trains for a question type that WBS13 is unlikely to set.

Misconceptions: organic-growth ('always safest') and staying-small ('means the firm failed') are genuine student errors. external-growth ('bigger is always better') is plausible. demergers ('demergers mean the firm failed') is filler given the topic itself is off-spec.
Notes[] only has 3 entries (Organic, External, Staying Small) so the Notes tab and Learn Mode disagree on scope (notes omit demergers), another sign the demerger subsection was bolted on.

3.2.1 Growth (a) Objectives of growth: economies of scale (internal and external, with named types: purchasing, technical, managerial, financial, marketing), increased market power over customers and suppliers, increased market share and brand recognition, increased profitability. Not taught; only in flashcards/extras and quizzed.

content.text: Fix the block↔assessment wiring: set each block's quizIndices/practiceIndices to MCQs and practice questions about that block (e.g. Inflation → Q5/practice[4]; Exchange/Interest/Tax → Q0/Q7/Q16/practice[0]; Business Cycle → Q1/Q8/Q13; Legislation → Q9/Q12/Q17; Competitive → Q6). Fix the Q15 '$1 = $1.30' typo and the Q5 double-correct option.

Internationalise for IAL: replace UK statutes, NICs, Bank of England and CMA with generic terms plus one non-UK example per idea; delete the examMatters claims that students 'must know' the Consumer Rights Act provisions and that examiners 'frequently use Porter's Five Forces'.

Teach the missing spec items instead of Economics extras: add subsections on government spending, economic uncertainty, environmental / competition / health-and-safety legislation, and market size / responses to a changing competitive environment; cut cost-push vs demand-pull and the perfect-competition→monopoly taxonomy to asides.

Add retrieval and a diagram: genuine-sequence reorders (interest-rate transmission chain; boom→recession→slump→recovery), a SPICED fillin, and a business-cycle diagram; wire them so the spaced/immediate recall slots are used in every step.

Rewrite practice to IAL formats with levels-based mark schemes (2-mark 'What is meant by', 4-mark 'Explain one', 8-mark 'Analyse', 10/12-mark 'Assess', 20-mark 'Evaluate'), all anchored to a short international case-study extract, and replace the shareholders-vs-stakeholders 20-marker with an external-influences one (e.g. evaluate whether a rise in interest rates is the biggest threat to Business X).

Whole section (all 12 subsections) — e.g. Exchange Rates body, Interest Rates body ('Bank of England sets the base rate'), Taxation body ('Employer National Insurance Contributions'), Consumer Protection body ('Consumer Rights Act 2015', 'Trade Descriptions Act', 'Consumer Contracts Regulations'), quiz Q4/Q12/Q14 (CMA, Employment Rights Act): Content is UK-GCE framed and presented as required IAL knowledge. IAL WBS12 questions use international contexts and mark schemes never require UK statute names, NICs, BoE or CMA. For a HK/Malaysia/Pakistan student this is both alienating and misleading about what earns marks.

Block 'Business Legislation' > consumer-protection-legislation > examMatters: Claims 'You must know the key provisions [of the Consumer Rights Act]... and explain the business's legal obligations'. IAL Business mark schemes credit generic understanding of consumer protection effects on a business, not UK statutory provisions.

Block 'The Competitive Environment' > competitive-pressures > body + examMatters ('Examiners frequently use Porter's Five Forces as a framework'): Porter's Five Forces is not in the Edexcel IAL Business specification (Unit 2 or elsewhere); the claim that examiners 'frequently use' it is false and steers students to an unrewarded framework.

Block 'Inflation' > cost-push-demand-pull-inflation > examMatters: 'Stating that inflation increases costs without distinguishing between cost-push and demand-pull shows a lack of analytical depth' — this is an Economics distinction; IAL Business mark schemes for inflation questions reward cost/margin/demand/uncertainty chains applied to the business, not inflation typology.
q15: Currency typo: should read '£1 = $1.30 to £1 = $1.40'. As written the stem is nonsensical and a student cannot tell which currency strengthened.
