content.text: The AD Curve > movements-along-ad > realExample: Claims 2022 UK inflation caused a movement along AD via three effects and lists 'pushed the Bank of England to raise interest rates (interest rate effect)'. The interest-rate effect behind AD's slope is the money-demand mechanism; a central bank raising the policy rate is a discretionary monetary tightening that SHIFTS AD left. The example therefore confuses the exact distinction the subsection exists to teach, and 2022 inflation was a cost-push (SRAS) episode, which the example never mentions.

The Accelerator Effect > accelerator-definition > realExample: Says UK car investment fell in 2017-18 'even though car sales were still at historically high levels' and that a 'slowdown in growth, not an actual decline' triggered it. UK new-car registrations peaked in 2016 (~2.69m) and fell in both 2017 (-5.7%) and 2018 (-6.8%), so demand actually declined. The example contradicts the mechanism it is meant to illustrate.

The Multiplier > multiplier-formula > body para 1 vs quiz Q21: Body defines MPC as 'the proportion of each extra pound ... spent on domestic goods and services' and says k = 1/(1-MPC) is 'equivalent' to 1/MPW. Under that definition it is; but quiz Q21 marks '1/(1-MPC)' WRONG for an open economy with government. The section teaches one thing and tests the opposite.

q21: Distractor [2] '1/(1-MPC)' is presented as wrong, but the section body defines MPC as spending 'on domestic goods and services' and states k = 1/(1-MPC) is 'equivalent' to 1/MPW. Under the section's own teaching two options are correct.

q8: Answer depends on knowing that 'Jobseeker's Allowance' is a UK unemployment benefit and that 'NHS' is a health service. International IAL students (HK, Korea, Pakistan) may not know either; the item then tests UK civics not economics.

p2: 'Analyse ... (10 marks)': in IAL WEC12 'Analyse' is an 8-mark question; 10 and 12 marks are 'Assess'/'Discuss' with evaluation. The scheme awards 4 of 10 marks for Marshall-Lerner and the J-curve, which are Unit 4 (WEC14) content, and lists point-by-point marks where IAL uses levels-based marking for 8+ mark items. No AD diagram is required, which an examiner would expect in KAA.

Inline diagrams never render: block 2 diagramRef 'Aggregate Demand Curve' and block 3 diagramRef 'Shifts in Aggregate Demand' do not substring-match any diagram title ('The AD Curve', 'The Multiplier Effect', 'Circular Flow of Income with AD Components') under the match in components/LearnModeTab.jsx:97-104 (t.includes(ref) || ref.includes(t)). Blocks 4 and 5 have no diagramRef even though 'The Multiplier Effect' exists. Net: 0 of 3 diagrams appear in Learn Mode for this section.

quizIndices are assigned sequentially [0],[1],[2],[3],[4] rather than by topic: block 'Shifts in AD' shows Q2 (multiplier calc, untaught yet), block 'The Accelerator Effect' shows Q4 (AD leftward shift). Only 5 of 25 MCQs are used inline; the two accelerator MCQs (Q7, Q15) are never used.

The 3-subsection 'The Multiplier' block duplicates national-income's 'The Multiplier and National Income' block (national-income uses ids multiplier-concept / multiplier-formula / multiplier-evaluation; this section uses multiplier-definition / multiplier-formula / multiplier-size-determinants -- 'multiplier-formula' is the same id in both files). IAL puts the multiplier under 2.3.4 National income. A student following the unit does the multiplier twice, and if any client-side state is keyed by subsection id it may collide.

Pre-test gate draws 3 random MCQs from a 25-item bank that includes circular-flow (Q9, Q18) and paradox-of-thrift (Q23) items not taught in this section, plus UK-institution items (Q8). A first-time learner can be gated on material the section never teaches -- consistent with the founder's 'pre-test demotivates' hypothesis.

Recall placement side-effect: single-section steps (multiplier-size-determinants, step 6) get their recall shown as 'immediate' at the bottom of that step AND as 'spaced' at the top of the next step, so the not-orderable 'order of logic' reorder is the one widget students meet twice in a row.

Misconception duplication: ad-formula-and-components and determinants-of-gov-spending-net-exports carry the same transfer-payments misconception almost verbatim. Otherwise misconceptions are genuine (MPC<1, 'AD falls' vs 'shifts left', micro substitution reasoning, multiplier != government revenue, accelerator vs multiplier).

Audience fit: 11 of 14 realExamples are UK-centric (house prices, Brexit, furlough, Bank of England, London 2012, OBR, UK car makers, UK 2008, UK 2020) for a HK/Korea/Singapore/Malaysia/Pakistan/Sri Lanka/Middle East cohort; only Apple and Singapore are non-UK. Not wrong for IAL marking, but a mismatch with the product's audience and its own 'international' positioning.

2-per-step pairing is coherent (formula+C; I+G/NX; shape+movements; right+left; concept+formula; size; accel def+cycle; limitations). Block takeaways match their blocks. Difficulty ramp (components -> curve -> shifts -> multiplier -> accelerator) is sensible, but the accelerator gets 3 of 14 subsections -- disproportionate for a topic that is at most an evaluation point, while spec bullets are missing (see ialSpecGaps).
Diagram SVGs hard-code light text (#e8ecf5) with a transparent background: legible only on a dark theme. If the app supports a light theme the axes and labels vanish.

2.3.2(a) relative importance of the components of AD -- only a UK % breakdown; no discussion of why C dominates, why I matters despite its size, or how composition differs (e.g. export-led Singapore/Korea vs consumption-led economies).

2.3.2(b) the distinction between saving and consumption (saving as the residual of disposable income; APC/APS/MPC/MPS) -- not taught in the consumption subsection; MPC only appears later inside the multiplier block.
2.3.2(c) gross vs net investment (depreciation/replacement investment) -- not taught, yet the accelerator block relies on 'net investment' undefined.
2.3.2(c) distinction between investment and saving -- only a one-clause aside ('does not include financial investments like buying shares').

2.3.2(c) influences on investment: 'Keynes and animal spirits' (examMatters only, never in body; tested by Q5), 'demand for exports', 'access to credit' (only as an accelerator limitation), 'influence of government and regulations' -- missing from the investment subsection.
2.3.2(d) government expenditure: G over the trade cycle (automatic stabilisers, counter-cyclical spending) -- one sentence only; fiscal policy link is thin.

2.3.2(e) net trade: effect of domestic real income on imports (income -> M), degree of protectionism, non-price factors (quality, design, reliability) -- missing; only exchange rate, relative inflation and foreign income are covered.
Multiplier ratio/process/MPC-MPS-MPT-MPM/calculation belong to 2.3.4 National income in the IAL spec; present here as a duplicate rather than a gap.
Accelerator: unsure whether the 2018 IAL WEC12 spec requires it explicitly under 2.3.2; treat as extension, not core, and reduce its weight.

Fix the fill-in data shape and renderer mismatch: split every template line to one '___' (changes-in-equilibrium, supply-side-shocks), replace compound tokens like 'rises, rises' with single words, and widen word banks beyond the answer list (add 2-3 distractors) so the 5 trivial fill-ins become real decisions; correct the five hint lengths.

Re-map inline quiz and practice to their blocks: set content[1].quizIndices to LRAS items (5/12/13/21), content[2] to 2/3/24, content[4] to 7/23/18; either stop sorting practice by marks in LearnModeTab.jsx line 80 or reorder practiceIndices so the SRAS block gets the SRAS movement-vs-shift question and the LRAS block gets the LRAS definition/outline; change practice[0] to a 2-mark 'Define' and practice[4] to 'Explain two factors'.

Add a fourth diagram titled to match 'Self-Correcting Mechanism' (negative gap closing via SRAS shift right, positive gap via SRAS left) and rename content[3].diagramRef so blocks 3 and 4 stop rendering without a diagram.

Correct the wrong/contradictory real examples: replace the 2022 UK manufacturers SRAS example, reword 'UK 2019 close to macroeconomic equilibrium' to 'close to full-employment output', fix the 'classical economics had not predicted stagflation' attribution, and use a demand-only case (2008-09 confidence collapse) instead of COVID in demand-side-shocks since applying-adas-to-events later says COVID shifted both curves.

De-duplicate: merge block 3 into block 2 (stagflation and AD-right analysis are taught twice), replace the two generic procedure reorders (ad-as-equilibrium, demand-side-shocks) with concrete causal chains, prune the quiz bank duplicates (Q11=Q1, Q13=Q5, Q14=Q4, Q19=Q8, Q24~Q18) and rewrite Q20 to name the Keynesian model; remove the 'SRAS steepens near capacity' takeaway so SRAS and Keynesian LRAS stay distinct.

content[0] 'Short-Run Aggregate Supply (SRAS)' > sras-shape-and-slope > realExample: Claims UK manufacturers in early 2022 saw margins boosted and expanded production because wages lagged output prices. 2022 was a cost-push squeeze (energy/input costs rose faster than output prices; UK manufacturing PMI fell below 50 from mid-2022 and output declined). The example illustrates the opposite of what happened.

content[2] 'Macroeconomic Equilibrium' > ad-as-equilibrium > realExample: Says the UK in 2019 'was operating close to macroeconomic equilibrium'. An economy is always at AD=AS equilibrium; what is meant is full-employment equilibrium. The section's own misconception two lines later warns that equilibrium is not the same as full employment, so the example teaches the misconception it is correcting.

p0: 'Define the term LRAS (4 marks)' — IAL Economics uses 'Define' for 2-mark items; 4-mark Section A/B items are 'Explain ...'. The guidance also awards marks for 'LRAS is vertical in the classical model' and 'shifts are caused by ...', which are not part of a definition. Mark allocation and mark scheme do not match IAL practice. Because LearnModeTab sorts practice by marks, this LRAS question is the inline practice for the SRAS block.

Inline quiz-to-block mapping is wrong: content[1] (LRAS) has quizIndices [1] which is an SRAS-shift question; content[2] (Equilibrium) gets Q2 (classical LR effect of AD, really LRAS material); content[4] (SR vs LR adjustment) gets Q5 (LRAS determinants). Only blocks 0 and 3 get a topically matching inline MCQ. Q7/Q23/Q24 (self-correction, sticky wages, output gap) are never shown inline.

Inline practice mapping is by mark size, not topic: LearnModeTab.jsx line 80 sorts practice by marks, so practiceIndices [0..4] resolve to Define-LRAS(4) on the SRAS block, Outline-LRAS(4) on the LRAS block, Explain-SRAS-movement-vs-shift(6) on the Equilibrium block, Assess-supply-side(10) on the Events block, Evaluate(20) on the Adjustment block. The mark ramp is sensible but three of five are off-topic for their block.

Two blocks get no inline diagram: diagramRef 'AD/AS Shifts' (content[3]) and 'Self-Correcting Mechanism' (content[4]) match no diagram title via the substring test in LearnModeTab.jsx lines 97-104 (titles are 'Short-Run Aggregate Supply (SRAS)', 'LRAS: Classical vs Keynesian', 'AD/AS Equilibrium: Multiple Scenarios'). There is no diagram anywhere of the self-correcting mechanism (SRAS shifting to close a gap), which is the most diagram-dependent idea in the section. Renaming content[3].diagramRef to 'AD/AS Equilibrium' would collide with content[2] (usedDiagrams set), so a fourth diagram is needed.

Recall duplication caused by odd section counts: blocks 1, 3 and 4 have 3 sections, so the third section is a solo step. For a solo step, the 'immediate' recall (first section of the step) and the next step's 'spaced' recall (last section of the previous step) are the same object — lras-determinants fillin and applying-adas-to-events reorder are each shown twice back-to-back (LearnModeTab.jsx lines 345-402).

Content repetition across blocks: stagflation is taught with near-identical flow chains in changes-in-equilibrium and supply-side-shocks; the AD-right analysis appears in changes-in-equilibrium and demand-side-shocks; classical vs Keynesian appears in block 1 (shapes) and block 4 (adjustment) with examMatters in keynesian-lras and classical-vs-keynesian-adjustment saying the same thing. Block 3 ('AD/AS Analysis of Macroeconomic Events') is largely a restatement of block 2 and could be merged, cutting the section from 13 to ~10 subsections — relevant given 75% of users never leave step 0.

Three of six reorders are the same generic exam-procedure list (ad-as-equilibrium, demand-side-shocks, applying-adas-to-events); only sras-shifts, keynesian-lras and self-correcting-mechanism test economics. Recall 'shuffled' arrays reuse two permutations ([2,0,3,1] x3, [3,1,0,2] x2), so a student who notices can solve by pattern.

Fill-in data shape not supported by the renderer: changes-in-equilibrium template lines 0-1 and supply-side-shocks template line 1 contain two '___' with a single compound answer ('rises, rises'); FillInRecall.jsx destructures split('___') into [before, after], dropping the second blank. Five of seven hints have character counts that do not match the answer length (education, stagflation, dilemma, inflationary, intervention).

Section scope vs label: titled '2.3.3 Aggregate Supply' but covers IAL 2.3.1-2.3.3 (AS characteristics, SRAS, LRAS) plus 2.4.3 (equilibrium real national output, blocks 2-3) plus 2.5.2 (output gaps, block 4). Students cross-referencing the spec will not find macro equilibrium or output gaps under 2.3.3.
content.note: SPEC NUMBERING: this item cites 2.4.3, 2.5.2, which is UK GCE A-level numbering and does not exist in the IAL spec. The IAL topic for this section is 2.3.3. Find the requirement by its wording in audit/raw/econ_spec.txt, not by the number. (noted 13 Sep 2026)

content.text: Takeaways match their blocks, with one exception: content[0] takeaway 'Near full capacity the SRAS curve becomes steeper' encodes the SRAS/Keynesian-LRAS conflation noted under accuracy. Misconceptions are mostly genuine student errors (higher prices shift SRAS; government spending shifts LRAS; Keynesian AS drawn flat; equilibrium = desirable; output gap = recession); the classical-vs-keynesian-adjustment one ('Keynesians say markets never work') is a straw man rather than an observed error.
Difficulty ramp is sensible (SRAS -> LRAS -> equilibrium -> shocks -> adjustment) and pairing classical-lras with keynesian-lras in one step is the right pedagogical choice.
2.3.3 LRAS factor 'changes in relative productivity' (productivity relative to other economies) — not taught; productivity appears only as a diagram annotation and a quiz distractor.
2.3.3 LRAS factor 'demographic changes and migration' — only the word 'immigration' inside one bullet in lras-determinants; no treatment of ageing populations, participation rates or emigration.

2.3.3 LRAS factor 'changes in government regulations' — only 'deregulation' listed inside the 'Institutional factors' bullet with no explanation of the mechanism (compliance costs, labour-market rules).
2.3.3 LRAS factor 'competition policy' — named in one bullet, never explained (how contestability raises efficiency/potential output).
2.3.1 'distinction between movement along and shift of the AS curve' is taught for SRAS only; not stated for LRAS (e.g. that there is no 'movement along' a vertical LRAS).
2.5.2 (if output gaps are intended to live here) 'difficulties of measuring output gaps' — not taught; the section presents potential output as observable.

content.text: Fix the plumbing so the section's own assets appear in the right place: make diagram matching hyphen/space-insensitive (or add an id to each diagram and reference it), make practiceIndices index the unsorted practice[] array (and include the 20-marker), and set quizIndices per block topically (e.g. Objectives → [15], Fiscal → [1], Monetary → [3], Supply-side → [5], Conflicts → [0]).

Replace the three non-orderable/arbitrary reorders (low-stable-inflation 'reasoning for 2%', market-based 'most to least direct', evaluating-supply-side 'by importance', plus merge the simultaneous steps in automatic-stabilisers) with genuine causal chains as suggested in recallAudit.

Rebuild the nine fillins so they cannot be solved by grammar: word banks of 5-6 with plausible economic distractors (right/left, appreciates/depreciates, short/long, positive/negative), drop the answer-defining parentheticals, and remove hints that spell out the answer ('2-_').

Correct the factual and consistency errors: UK 1970s unemployment claim, the non-existent UK 2% growth target, unify the transmission lag figure across notes/diagram/practice, and note Phillips' original curve was wage inflation.

Bring the practice bank into IAL form: definitions at 2 marks, replace 'Outline', remove 'in the UK' framing, and rewrite the 10- and 20-mark guidance as levels-based KAA/Evaluation with an expected diagram; then add short teaching on the untaught spec bullets (other objectives, deficit vs debt, Great Depression/2008 policy responses, policies vs improvements).

content[4] 'Policy Conflicts and Trade-Offs' > phillips-curve > realExample: 'The UK in the 1970s experienced stagflation with unemployment and inflation both exceeding 10%.' UK inflation did exceed 10% (peaking ~24% in 1975) but UK unemployment stayed roughly 3-6% through the 1970s and only passed 10% in 1981-82. The stagflation point stands; the number is wrong.

q0: Content is fine, but via content[0].quizIndices=[0] this MCQ is rendered as the end-of-block quiz for 'Macroeconomic Objectives', before the Phillips curve is taught (block 4). Also near-duplicate of Q8 and Q13.

p0: 'Define the term fiscal policy (4 marks)'. IAL definitions are 2 marks; the 4-mark guidance awards marks for expansionary/contractionary and 'announced in the annual Budget', which is not what a definition mark scheme rewards. Either make it 2 marks or turn it into 'Explain, using an example, how fiscal policy can influence AD (4 marks)'.

p2: 'Assess the effectiveness of supply-side policies in reducing unemployment in the UK (10 marks)'. Tariff/command word match IAL. But (a) guidance is point-marked (2+2+2+1+1+1+1) whereas IAL 10-mark 'Assess' is levels-marked KAA (6) + Evaluation (4); (b) 'in the UK' is GCE framing — IAL questions refer to the data context or 'an economy of your choice'; (c) no diagram expectation (LRAS shift or Phillips curve) although IAL 10-markers reward one.

No diagram renders in Learn Mode for this section: diagramRefs 'fiscal-policy-ad', 'monetary-policy-transmission', 'supply-side-lras', 'phillips-curve' are matched by substring against titles 'Fiscal Policy: AD/AS Impact', 'Monetary Policy Transmission Mechanism', 'Supply-Side Policy: LRAS Shift', 'The Phillips Curve' (LearnModeTab.jsx:97-104: t.includes(ref) || ref.includes(t)); hyphens vs spaces means all four fail silently. Verified by simulation. Four good diagrams with checklists are wasted; the Phillips curve block teaches 'draw both curves' with no picture.

Practice questions land on the wrong blocks: practiceIndices index into sortedPractice (sorted by marks, LearnModeTab.jsx:80), so block 1 Fiscal → 'Define fiscal policy' (OK by luck), block 2 Monetary → 'Outline two supply-side policies', block 3 Supply-Side → 'Explain two conflicts between objectives', block 4 Conflicts → 'Assess supply-side policies... unemployment'. The 20-mark monetary policy essay (sorted index 4) is never shown.

Inline quizzes are sequential (quizIndices [0],[1],[2],[3],[4]) rather than topical: block 0 Objectives gets a Phillips-curve MCQ (untaught until block 4), block 2 Monetary gets crowding out (fiscal), block 3 Supply-Side gets monetary transmission, block 4 Conflicts gets QE. Only block 1 (automatic stabiliser) matches. Should be e.g. [15 or 8], [1 or 21], [3 or 4], [5 or 16], [0 or 19].

Redundancy within block 2: interest-rate-policy body[3] already lists all four transmission channels and the 12-18 month lag; monetary-transmission-mechanism then re-teaches the same four channels. Their two fillins share the answer 'asset'. Merge, or make interest-rate-policy about the rate decision/inflation target and leave channels to the transmission section.

Block 0 'conflicts-between-objectives' (step 3, rendered alone) substantially overlaps with the whole of block 4; its fillin recall demands 'Phillips' although the body never mentions the Phillips curve.

Pairing: block 0 has 5 sections so 'conflicts-between-objectives' sits alone on a step that also carries the block's takeaway, quiz, practice and ExplainItBack — heaviest step in the section for the thinnest content. Blocks 1-4 (3 sections each) pair (a,b) then (c) alone; acceptable.

Misconceptions in evaluating-supply-side, policy-trade-offs-evaluation, conflicts-between-objectives and monetary-transmission-mechanism are exam-technique notes ('students list without judgement', 'students describe only one channel'), not conceptual misconceptions; the other 13 are genuine (zero inflation ideal, 0% unemployment, deficit always bad, QE = government printing money, permanent Phillips trade-off).

Real-example bias: 8 of 17 examples are UK, 3 US, 1 EU, and none from Asia/Middle East for an audience in HK/Korea/Singapore/Malaysia/Pakistan. IAL Unit 2 data-response extracts routinely use non-UK economies; examples such as Japan's QE/zero rates, Singapore's exchange-rate-based monetary policy, Korea's interventionist industrial strategy, Pakistan/Sri Lanka current-account crises would land better.

Takeaways match their blocks. Difficulty ramp (objectives → fiscal → monetary → supply → Phillips) is sensible; the section is long (17 subsections, ~11 steps plus 17 recalls plus pre/post tests) and would benefit from trimming the two redundancies above.

Objectives beyond the four taught: balanced government budget, protection of the environment, greater income equality are listed IAL 2.3.6 objectives; none is taught (growth vs environment appears only as a quiz distractor).

Distinction between government budget (fiscal) deficit/surplus and national debt as a stock — mentioned in one sentence (fiscal-policy-tools body[3]) and quiz 18; no definition of national debt or stock/flow framing.
Role of the central bank vs the government in demand-side policy (independence, inflation-target remit) — only implicit; the practice[3] guidance mentions independence but the notes do not.

Use of demand-side policies in the Great Depression and the 2008 global financial crisis — explicit IAL bullet; not taught (the 2021 US stimulus and 2009-21 QE examples are adjacent but the Depression/2008 comparison is absent). Fairly confident this is in the IAL spec; flag as 'verify'.

Strengths and weaknesses of demand-side policies: fiscal time lags, crowding out, liquidity trap, effect of MPC/imports on the multiplier are tested in quiz (2, 24) and practice (3) but not taught in body.
Distinction between supply-side policies and supply-side improvements — not taught.

Supply-side policies 'to promote competition' and 'to increase incentives' are named only as one-word list items; no mechanism for competition policy (e.g. competition law, reducing barriers to entry).

Potential policy conflicts (as opposed to objective conflicts) — e.g. fiscal expansion vs monetary tightening, supply-side tax cuts worsening the budget — only glancingly covered in policy-trade-offs-evaluation.

Unsure: whether IAL 2.3.6 expects the expectations-augmented Phillips curve explicitly (taught here) — GCE Theme 2 does not, IAL may not; if not, the block 4 depth is beyond spec, which is fine but the 'most frequently examined' claims should go.

Make diagrams appear in Learn Mode: rename diagramRefs to match titles (e.g. 'trade cycle', 'output gap', 'ppf') or fix the matcher in LearnModeTab.jsx:97-104 to normalise hyphens/spaces; add the PPF diagram to Block 1 and the output-gap diagram to Block 2.

Rewrite the six weak/not-orderable recalls: replace costs-growth-environment and supply-side-causes rankings with classification exercises, fix the cyclic four-phase reorder by anchoring a start point, collapse the duplicated LRAS-chain reorder, and replace trivial collocation fill-ins (actual-economic-growth, relationship-actual-potential, demand-side-causes, benefits-growth, growth-living-standards) with banks where two words genuinely compete.

Fix practice: remove the Unit 4 FDI question, change 'Define (4 marks)' to a 2-mark define or a 4-mark explain, change 'Outline' to 'Explain', map practice to blocks by topic rather than sorted mark index, and rewrite 10/20-mark guidance as levels-based KAA/evaluation descriptors with a required diagram.

Correct the accuracy slips a teacher would catch: 'movement along the PPF' → 'from inside towards the PPF'; 'elastic section of SRAS' → consistent Keynesian/classical model; 'falling real wages' in a positive gap; standardise cycle-phase names across text, diagram and extras.

Trim redundancy and add missing spec content: merge Block 6 into Blocks 1 and 4, dedupe the quiz bank (Q9/Q20, Q16, Q21, Q23) and replace duplicates with items on export-led growth, trend growth, and impact on firms / current-vs-future living standards, which are currently untaught.

Actual vs Potential Economic Growth > actual-economic-growth > examMatters: Says to 'link actual growth to a movement along the PPF'. Actual growth from spare capacity is a movement from INSIDE the PPF towards it; a movement ALONG the PPF is reallocation, which quiz Q3's own explanation says 'is not growth'. Content contradicts its own quiz.

p0: 'Define the term economic growth (4 marks)' — IAL Economics 'Define' questions are 2 marks (definition + development). A 4-mark item would be 'Explain...' or a Section A supported MCQ (1 + 3). The guidance awards marks for the actual/potential distinction and measurement method, which a 'define' does not invite. This is also the item Learn Mode surfaces first (sortedPractice index 0, 'worked' mode) so it sets the wrong expectation.

p2: 'Assess the importance of FDI in promoting economic growth in developing countries (10 marks)' is WEC14 Unit 4 (development/FDI) content, not Unit 2 economic growth. Additionally the guidance is a points list summing to 10 (2+2+2+1+1+1+1), whereas IAL 10-mark 'Assess' is levels-marked (KAA and evaluation levels). Never shown in Learn Mode either (practiceIndices only reach sorted indices 0-2).

NO diagrams render in Learn Mode for this section. LearnModeTab.jsx:97-104 matches step.diagramRef to diagram titles by case-insensitive substring; block refs are 'ad-as-growth', 'output-gap-diagram', 'trade-cycle-diagram', 'ad-as-shifts', 'ad-as-growth-analysis' (hyphenated) while titles are 'The Business (Trade) Cycle', 'Output Gap Diagram', 'PPF: Actual vs Potential Growth' (spaces). Verified: zero matches for all six blocks. For a topic whose exam value is almost entirely diagrammatic (PPF, AD/AS, trade cycle), students see three well-drawn diagrams only on the Diagrams tab. The PPF diagram, ideal for Block 1, is never referenced by any block; Block 5 has no diagramRef at all.

Block 6 'Economic Growth and AD/AS Analysis' re-teaches Block 1 (actual = AD shift, potential = LRAS shift) and Block 4 (demand-side vs supply-side) a third time, with a duplicated reorder (potential-economic-growth vs lras-shifts-growth) and near-identical flows. 17 subsections / 11 Learn Mode steps for one spec point is long; merging Block 6 into Blocks 1 and 4 would cut ~3 steps without losing content.

Sequencing within Block 3: the four-phase overview of the cycle is introduced in the THIRD subsection ('Recovery and Stages of the Cycle', body para 2) after Boom and Recession have already been taught. The overview (and the trade-cycle diagram) should open the block.

2-per-step pairing: Block 1 = [actual, potential], [relationship]; Block 2 = [positive, negative], [implications]; Block 3 = [boom, recession], [recovery]; Block 4 = [demand, supply]; Block 5 = [benefits, env costs], [living standards]; Block 6 = [AD, LRAS], [combined]. Pairs are coherent, but every 3-section block ends with a lone-section step carrying diagram + quiz + practice + explain-back + takeaway, making the final step of each block much heavier than the others.

Practice mapping is by sorted-marks index not by topic: Block 3 (trade cycle) gets 'Define economic growth' (4m), Block 4 (causes) gets 'Outline actual vs potential' (4m), Block 5 gets 'Explain two costs' (6m, the only topical match). The 10-mark and 20-mark items are never reached in Learn Mode.

quizIndices only reference Q0-Q5; Q6-Q23 appear only in PreTest/PostTest sampling and the Quiz tab. Since the pre-test samples 3 random from 24 mostly-duplicate items, the pre/post comparison is noisy.

Misconceptions: most are genuine (positive gap = good; recovery = back to normal; demand-side growth always inflationary; growth always harms environment; GDP = living standards). Filler ones: relationship-actual-potential ('students treat them as separate topics that never interact'), lras-shifts-growth ('students forget to explain the cause' — exam-technique, not a misconception), supply-side-causes ('students don't distinguish quantity and quality').

Takeaways match their blocks. Block 6's fourth takeaway ('Always label diagrams fully...') is exam advice rather than content; Block 5's takeaway omits the current-account cost that quiz Q5 and common_mistakes[1] both treat as a standard cost.
Terminology drift between surfaces (content vs diagram vs extras) on cycle phase names, and between quiz Q6 and Q16 on 'sustainable growth' (see accuracy/quiz).

Learn Mode fill-ins use a 3-word bank (FillInRecall.jsx:12) so almost every fillin in this section collapses to grammar/elimination; the design, not just this section's authoring, makes 'trivial' the default verdict.

Export-led growth / importance of international trade for economic growth — in the IAL 'causes of economic growth' bullet; only appears as quiz Q14, never taught in content[] (Australia example touches commodity exports but does not name the concept).
Trend rate of growth (actual growth vs trend/long-run growth rate) — only in quiz Q8 and the diagram legend; not defined in content.

Impact of growth on FIRMS (profits, investment, but also rising costs/wages, competition) — 'impact of economic growth on consumers, firms, government, current and future living standards' is the spec framing; firms get one sentence on 'business confidence'.

Current vs future living standards trade-off (consumption vs capital goods on the PPF; growth today at the cost of tomorrow) — not explicitly framed, though the PPF diagram axes (capital vs consumer goods) would support it.
Current account deterioration as a cost of growth — taught only in quiz Q5, common_mistakes[1] and a positive-output-gap examMatters aside; absent from Block 5 'Costs and Benefits'.
Inflation as a cost of growth is in extras/practice but not in Block 5's costs subsection (it is in Block 2's positive-gap subsection, so partially covered).

Unsure: the product numbers this '2.3.5'; my recollection is that IAL WEC12 places economic growth under its own heading (causes / output gaps / trade cycle / impact) rather than under 2.3 aggregate supply — verify numbering against the current IAL specification.

Add diagramRef/quizIndices/practiceIndices to all 4 blocks so the objectives and principal-agent diagrams actually render, the integration diagram moves to 'Growth of Firms', each inline MCQ/practice matches its block, and the 20-mark Evaluate is reachable (currently everything is mis-placed by the legacy fallback in components/learn-mode/utils.js).

Add recall exercises to every subsection (fillin for the three objective conditions and liability types; reorder for the principal-agent → satisficing chain and the horizontal-merger → concentration → regulator chain).

Correct the Amazon example (revenue/growth maximisation, reinvested profits, dollars), internationalise the regulator references (not just CMA), and align practice command words/tariffs with IAL (Define = 2 marks, drop 'Outline', describe levels-based marking for the 10- and 20-mark items).

content[3] 'Economies and Diseconomies of Scale' > diseconomies-demergers > realExample: 'eBay demerged Skype in 2009, selling it to Microsoft' is wrong on two counts. (1) Fact: in 2009 eBay sold a ~65-70% stake to an investor group led by Silver Lake; Microsoft bought Skype in 2011 for $8.5bn. (2) Concept: selling a subsidiary to a third party is a divestment/sell-off, not a demerger (a demerger spins the unit off into a separately listed company whose shares go to existing shareholders). This is the section's only demerger example and it teaches the wrong definition.

content.text: content[0] 'Business Objectives' > alternative-objectives > realExample: Amazon example muddles the terminology just taught: it says Amazon 'prioritised revenue and market share' then calls this 'sales maximisation' (AR = AC breakeven). Amazon's strategy was long-run growth/revenue maximisation and it was profitable most years after 2003. Also 'reinvesting every pound of revenue' — Amazon is a US firm and you reinvest profit/cash flow, not revenue.
q6: Co-operatives are never mentioned in content[], notes[] or flashcards[]; this MCQ (which can appear in the pre-test gate) tests untaught material. The question itself is sound.

No content block has diagramRef, quizIndices or practiceIndices, so LearnModeTab.jsx:86 takes the legacy fallback (components/learn-mode/utils.js). Consequences for this section: (a) matchDiagramsToBlocks finds no title-word overlap for 'Profit Maximisation, Revenue Maximisation and Sales Volume Maximisation' or 'Principal-Agent Problem (Divorce of Ownership from Control)' with any block title, so 2 of 3 diagrams are never shown in Learn Mode; (b) 'Types of Business Growth (Integration)' scores 2 against 'Types of Business Organisation' vs 1 against 'Growth of Firms', so the integration diagram is shown on the sole-trader/Ltd block; (c) distributeItems puts quiz[0..3] on steps 0..3 (horizontal integration on Business Objectives, profit max on Types of Organisation, sales max on Growth of Firms, principal-agent on Economies of Scale) and never shows quiz[4..9]; (d) practice sorted by marks gives step0=Define limited liability, step1=Outline demerger, step2=Explain horizontal, step3=Assess principal-agent, and the 20-mark Evaluate is never shown. Fix: add diagramRef/quizIndices/practiceIndices to each block.

Zero recall exercises across 8 subsections (meta.reorder=0, meta.fillin=0), so the spaced/immediate recall mechanic of Learn Mode is inert for this section and the CompletionScreen recall score is always 0/0. Good candidates: fillin on 'profit max where MC = __, revenue max where MR = __, sales max where AR = __'; reorder on the principal-agent chain (ownership separated from control → managers pursue own goals → imperfect information → satisficing).

Block ordering front-loads 'Business Objectives' and invokes 'principal-agent problem' and 'ownership separated from control' (alternative-objectives) before 'divorce of ownership and control' is actually explained in block 2 (limited-companies). Either swap blocks 1 and 2 (types of organisation → objectives) or add a one-line definition in alternative-objectives.

Block 4 'Economies and Diseconomies of Scale' belongs to IAL 3.3.2 (Revenue, costs and profits) and the notes[] for this section already contain a full Economies of Scale note; the content spends 2 of 8 subsections on it while genuine 3.3.1 material (public/private sector, not-for-profit, why firms stay small, constraints on growth, demerger impacts) is absent. Only the demerger half of block 4 is on-spec for 3.3.1.

2-per-step pairing is coherent (each block is exactly 2 sections = 1 step), so the section is only 4 steps long; with 4 steps the takeaways align with their blocks. Takeaway block 4 references MES, which the body never defines.

The pre-test draws 3 random MCQs from a bank where 2 of 10 items (co-operatives, constraints on growth) test content the section never teaches, so a student can be told they 'don't know' material the lesson will not cover.

Misconceptions are mostly genuine (revenue max vs profit max; limited liability vs limited risk; economies = average not total cost; sole traders always small). 'Students assume mergers always create synergies' and 'diseconomies inevitable for all large firms' are weaker/filler-ish but not wrong.

Difficulty ramp is fine within blocks 1-3; block 4 is a restatement of easier material. No ExplainItBack prompts or diagram-drawing tasks tied to the objectives diagram, which examMatters calls 'the single most important diagram skill in Unit 3'.
Reasons why some firms tend to remain small and why others grow (niche/market size, owner objectives, access to finance, diseconomies) — not taught in content[]; only common_mistakes[3] mentions it.
Public sector vs private sector organisations — absent entirely.
Profit vs not-for-profit organisations (charities, co-operatives, social enterprises) — absent from content, yet quiz[6] tests co-operatives.
Constraints on business growth (size of market, access to finance, owner objectives, regulation) — not in content[]; quiz[4] tests it.
Reasons for and impact of demergers on businesses, workers and consumers — only 'reasons' touched in one paragraph; impacts on workers/consumers not covered.

Advantages and disadvantages of each type of integration (esp. vertical: securing supply/quality/foreclosure; conglomerate: lack of expertise, no synergies) — compressed into a single paragraph with no evaluation per type.

Divorce of ownership from control as an explicit spec term with its diagrammatic/objective consequences — present, but the objectives diagram is not surfaced in Learn Mode (unsure whether IAL 3.3.1 lists the diagram explicitly; the objectives bullets themselves are covered).

Add diagramRef, quizIndices and practiceIndices to each block (and split into 6-8 single-idea blocks) so Learn Mode stops using the legacy fallback: today diagrams[2] (LRAC) and diagrams[3] (shutdown), quiz[4..9] and the 20-mark essay never appear, and the MCQs/practice that do appear sit on the wrong block.

Add two teaching subsections for the untaught-but-tested 3.3.2 content: 'Economies and diseconomies of scale' (internal types, external, causes of diseconomies, link to LRAC/MES) and 'Shutdown points' (P < AVC in SR, P < AC in LR, MC above AVC as supply curve), wiring diagrams[3], quiz[4/5/7] and practice[1/4] to them.

Replace the two factually wrong real examples: British Airways (airline pricing is the opposite of what is stated) and OpenAI (has never earned supernormal profit). Also qualify 'competitive pressure forces firms to be productively efficient' to perfect competition only.

Add recall objects: reorder recalls from the existing flow chains (profit-max four-step method; supernormal-profit-entry chain; MC < ATC → average falls → MC crosses at min) and fill-ins for MR = a − 2bQ / MC cuts ATC at ___ / shut down if P < ___ — the section currently has zero retrieval practice.

Rewrite practice mark schemes to IAL format: 2-mark definition (not 4), replace 'Outline' with 'Explain', and present the 10-mark Assess and 20-mark Evaluate guidance as levels-based KAA + Evaluation with an explicit diagram requirement, instead of '(2 marks)' per bullet.

content[0] 'Revenue Concepts' > total-average-marginal-revenue > realExample: 'Airlines like British Airways use dynamic pricing — early bookers pay high fares (elastic segment, high MR), but as the flight fills, last-minute seats are sold cheaply.' This is backwards: airlines sell early seats cheaply and raise fares as departure approaches to capture inelastic late/business demand. It is also price discrimination (multiple prices, segmented demand), not a movement along a single AR/MR curve, so it does not illustrate the MR > 0 / MR < 0 point being taught.

content[2] 'Profit' > normal-supernormal-profit > realExample: 'When OpenAI demonstrated massive demand for generative AI, the supernormal profits attracted Google, Meta...' OpenAI has reported large losses every year (billions in 2023-25); it has never earned supernormal profit. Also 'supernormal profit does not last when barriers to entry are low' is applied to an industry with extreme capital barriers, which undercuts the point.

q4: Tests types of internal economies of scale (technical/financial/marketing/purchasing) — none of which are taught anywhere in content[]. Appears in pre-test and post-test as if it were section content.
q5: External vs internal economies of scale are not taught in content[] (the only 'economies of scale' mention is one sentence in short-run-long-run-costs). Untaught but tested.

q7: The shutdown rule (P < AVC short run, P < AC long run) is not taught in content[] — it exists only in diagrams[3], common_mistakes[3] and a flashcard, and diagrams[3] is never surfaced in Learn Mode (see structureIssues). Distractor D 'MC > MR at all output levels' is nonsensical rather than plausibly wrong.

Zero recall widgets: none of the 8 subsections has a `recall` object, so Learn Mode shows no reorder/fill-in retrieval at all for this section — the only active element per step is one MCQ + one written question. Given the section is diagram- and rule-heavy, the natural recalls are missing: a genuine sequence exists for the profit-max four-step method (MC=MR → Q* → P* from AR → compare AR to ATC) and for the supernormal-profit-entry chain (TR>TC → entry → supply up, price down → normal profit); fill-ins for 'MR = a − 2bQ', 'MC cuts ATC at its ___ point', 'shut down in SR if P < ___'.

No block carries diagramRef / quizIndices / practiceIndices, so LearnModeTab.jsx:86 `hasRefs` is false and the legacy fallback runs. Consequences computed from utils.js: (a) matchDiagramsToBlocks only places diagrams[0] 'Revenue Curves' on block 0 and diagrams[1] 'Short-Run Cost Curves' on block 1; diagrams[2] 'Long-Run Average Cost Curve' and diagrams[3] 'Short-Run and Long-Run Shutdown Points' share no title word with 'Profit' or 'Efficiency' and are NEVER shown in Learn Mode. (b) distributeItems(10 MCQs, 4 steps) puts quiz[0..3] on steps 0..3: quiz[1] (MR = 0, revenue) lands on the Cost block, quiz[2] (diminishing returns) on the Profit block, quiz[3] (MC cuts AC) on the Efficiency block; quiz[4..9] never appear. (c) sortedPractice by marks = [Define MR 4, Outline shutdown 4, Explain EoS 6, Assess dim. returns 10, Evaluate 20]; steps get Define MR (worked, block Revenue — fine), Outline shutdown (guided, on Cost block — topic untaught), Explain EoS (guided, on Profit block — untaught, wrong block), Assess diminishing returns (independent, on Efficiency block — wrong block); the 20-mark essay never appears.

Every block has exactly 2 sections, so the whole section is 4 steps, each ~900-1000 words (2 full sections + diagram + MCQ + practice + Explain-it-back + takeaway). Each step is simultaneously first- and last-in-block, so the spaced/immediate recall scaffolding has nothing to attach to. Recommend splitting into 6-8 blocks (Revenue; Revenue by market structure; SR costs; LR costs + economies of scale; Profit + shutdown; Profit max; Efficiency) so that each step is one idea and the last-of-block activities are topical.

Block 4 'Efficiency' (allocative, productive, dynamic, X-inefficiency) is IAL 3.3.3 'Market structures and contestability' content, not 3.3.2; it belongs after perfect competition/monopoly are taught. Meanwhile the 3.3.2 bullets actually missing (economies of scale types, shutdown points) are absent — the block budget is spent on the wrong topic.

content[] vs the rest of the section is internally inconsistent: notes[] has 8 headings including 'Long-Run Cost Curves' (which does cover EoS types) and 'Alternative Objectives on a Diagram' (3.3.1 material), common_mistakes[3] covers the shutdown rule, flashcards cover economies of scope and accounting vs economic profit — none of which the Learn Mode content teaches. A student who only uses Learn Mode is under-prepared for this section's own quiz.

Difficulty ramp inside Block 1 is inverted for weaker students: the twice-gradient/elasticity/MR-negative material (subsection 1) precedes the simpler price-taker vs price-maker distinction (subsection 2). Teaching AR = MR = P for a price taker first, then introducing the downward-sloping AR/MR, is the conventional and easier order.

Takeaways match their blocks and are accurate. Misconceptions are real ones (MR below AR in PC, diminishing returns vs diseconomies, normal profit = 'no profit', profit max vs revenue max, 'monopoly always bad'); only the first ('MR falls because the firm sells more') is slightly contrived. Flow chains are genuine causal sequences — these would convert well into reorder recalls.

Economies and diseconomies of scale as a full topic: types of internal economies (technical, managerial, purchasing/bulk-buying, financial, marketing, risk-bearing), external economies of scale, causes of diseconomies (communication, coordination, motivation) — only one sentence in content; tested in quiz[4], quiz[5], practice[1].

Short-run and long-run shutdown points (P < AVC shut down in SR; P < AC exit in LR; firm's SR supply curve = MC above AVC) — tested in quiz[7], practice[4], diagrams[3], common_mistakes[3], but not taught in content.

Calculation of TR, TC, AC, MC, profit from numerical data/tables — the IAL data-response regularly asks for calculations; no numeric worked example anywhere in content (quiz[0] is the only calculation).

Law of diminishing marginal productivity via marginal and average product (MP/AP curves and their link to MC/AVC) — content asserts diminishing returns raise MC but never shows product curves or a numeric example.

Loss-making firm diagram (AR < ATC) and the profit/loss rectangles for a price maker — profit-max subsection describes the four-step method but the only shaded-profit diagram (diagrams[3]) is perfect-competition and is not surfaced in Learn Mode.

Add diagramRef/quizIndices/practiceIndices to all four blocks so Learn Mode stops using the legacy fallback: block0 → diagrams 'Perfect Competition — Long-Run' (and/or short-run) + quiz [1,3] + practice [0]; block1 → 'Kinked Demand' + quiz [4,7] + practice [3]; block2 → 'Monopoly' + quiz [5] + practice [1,2]; block3 → quiz [8] + practice [4]. Fix the three broken diagram SVGs: redraw PC long-run and monopolistic-competition long-run so AR is genuinely tangent to a clean U-shaped AC (currently AR sits above AC and Qeff is not at min AC), and recompute the monopoly diagram's MR=MC, Pm, Qc and DWL polygon from actual curve intersections. Add a third-degree PD two-market diagram that examMatters already promises.

Close the spec gaps that the quiz already tests: add subsections (or a fifth block) for Monopsony (characteristics, stakeholder costs/benefits), Natural monopoly, X-inefficiency (moved to a short 'Efficiency' opener before perfect competition), barrier-to-entry types, and n-firm concentration ratios; then either remove quiz[2] (shutdown) or teach it. This alone removes the ~75% chance the pre-test contains untaught items.

Add recall exercises (currently zero): reorder recalls from the existing flows (perfect-competition entry chain; game-theory cartel-collapse chain; monopoly MC=MR→AR→DWL chain; contestability hit-and-run chain) and fillin recalls for the three PD conditions and the PC/mon-comp long-run conditions.

Correct the factual/exam-format errors: Ryanair/easyJet 'lease rather than buy' (wrong — use IndiGo/AirAsia or drop), '25-mark essays' → 20-mark IAL Section C, Nigeria as OPEC over-producer → Iraq/Kazakhstan, Morrisons in the 'big four' → Aldi (2022), soften 'zero dynamic efficiency' in PC; remove the kinked-demand-as-game-theory point from practice[3]'s model answer; and swap at least half the UK examples for HK/SE-Asia/Middle-East equivalents.

diagrams[3] 'Monopolistic Competition — Long-Run Equilibrium' (svg + checklist): The SVG does not draw a tangency. AC path (M110,100 Q200,195 280,165 Q340,152 440,185) has its minimum at roughly x=240,y=172 and then rises to a hump near x=320 before falling again at high output (an AC curve that falls at high output is malformed). At the marked 'tangency' E (225,148) the AR line is at y≈158 and AC at y≈171, so AR sits ~13px above AC — the picture shows supernormal profit, exactly what the section's own examMatters says 'examiners penalise'. 'Qeff' is drawn at x=295 but the AC minimum is at x≈240, so the 'Excess Capacity' bracket is measured to the wrong point.

diagrams[1] 'Perfect Competition — Long-Run Equilibrium' (svg + checklist): Same defect: AC path (M110,120 Q200,220 270,170 Q320,155 430,200) has its minimum near x≈226,y≈186, then rises to y≈166 near x≈305 and falls again. The AR = MR = P line at y=160 lies above AC everywhere (AR > AC), so the diagram depicts supernormal profit, not the 'tangent at minimum AC, normal profit only' the checklist claims; E at (270,160) is not on the AC curve (AC at x=270 is y=170).

diagrams[2] 'Monopoly — Profit-Maximising Equilibrium' (svg): Markers are not on the curves. MR line (90,40)->(270,280) and the MC segment through (200,200)-(280,100) intersect at ≈(205,193), but the MR=MC dot is at (210,170) — ~23px above the intersection. Pm on AR at x=210 should be y≈122 but is drawn at 108. AR=MC (competitive output) is at ≈(244,145) but Qc/the DWL apex is placed at (290,153), where AR is at y≈177 and MC at y≈88 — so the shaded DWL triangle (210,108)-(290,153)-(210,170) is not the area between AR and MC. This is the diagram examMatters calls 'the most important in the entire unit' and it IS the one shown in Learn Mode (block 2 via title-match fallback).

Contestable Markets > contestable-markets-theory > realExample: 'Airlines like Ryanair and easyJet lease aircraft rather than buying them' — Ryanair overwhelmingly owns its fleet (bulk Boeing 737 purchases; leasing is a small minority), and easyJet owns roughly two-thirds. The factual hook used to illustrate low sunk costs is wrong for the named firms.

Contestable Markets > evaluating-market-structures > examMatters: 'Top-band 25-mark essays' — 25-mark essays are UK GCE A-level (Papers 1/2/3). IAL WEC13 Section C essays are 20 marks; Section B data-response sub-questions top out at 12. Presents UK-GCE exam format as IAL.

q9: Monopsony is entirely absent from content[], notes[] and flashcards for this section, yet is an IAL spec bullet and a pre-test candidate. Explanation also mislabels: it says 'MCL' (marginal cost of labour) and 'marginal benefit' although the question is about a generic input buyer — should be 'marginal cost of the input (MC of purchasing) = MRP'.

p3: 20-mark 'Evaluate the usefulness of game theory' guidance awards marks for 'game theory explains real-world phenomena such as price rigidity — the kinked demand curve model' — the kinked demand curve is NOT a game-theory model, and common_mistakes[2] in this very section warns students not to conflate them. The model answer commits the section's own listed mistake. Also point-based (2+3+2+2+3+2+2+2+2) whereas IAL 20-markers are levels-marked (KAA + evaluation levels); no indication of the KAA/evaluation split.

Zero recall widgets (meta.reorder = 0, meta.fillin = 0; no section has a 'recall' key). Learn Mode's spaced/immediate retrieval layer renders nothing for this section — the flow is read → one MCQ → one practice per block. The flows (e.g. perfect-competition 'supernormal profit → entry → supply up → price falls → normal profit', game-theory 'cartel → temptation → cheat → collapse') are genuine causal sequences that would make good reorder exercises.

No block has diagramRef/quizIndices/practiceIndices, so LearnModeTab.jsx:114-118 uses the legacy fallback. matchDiagramsToBlocks (components/learn-mode/utils.js:31) title-matches: diagrams[0] PC short-run → block 0, diagrams[2] Monopoly → block 2, diagrams[4] Kinked → block 1; diagrams[1] 'Perfect Competition — Long-Run Equilibrium' and diagrams[3] 'Monopolistic Competition — Long-Run Equilibrium' find no unused block and are NEVER shown in Learn Mode — even though perfect-competition.examMatters ('practise showing the shift from short-run supernormal profit to long-run normal profit') and monopolistic-competition.examMatters ('the key diagram skill is drawing the long-run tangency') name those exact diagrams. Block 3 (Contestable Markets) gets no diagram.

Quiz fallback (distributeItems, utils.js:12-13): 12 items ≥ 4 steps so quiz[0..3] land on steps 0..3: step 1 (Oligopoly) shows 'In the long run in perfect competition...', step 2 (Monopoly) shows 'shutdown point', step 3 (Contestable) shows the monopolistic-competition excess-capacity item. The kinked-demand (4), price-discrimination (5), Nash (7) and contestability (8) MCQs — the ones that match blocks 1–3 — never appear inline.

Practice fallback: sortedPractice by marks = [Define PC 4, Outline contestable 4, Explain PD 6, Assess monopoly 10, Evaluate game theory 20]; steps 0–3 get items 0–3, so the Oligopoly step gets the contestable-markets question, the Contestable step gets the monopoly Assess, and the 20-mark game-theory essay (the only one matching block 1) is never surfaced. getPracticeMode then makes the mismatched Oligopoly item the 'guided' one.

Sequencing: allocative/productive/dynamic efficiency are used from perfect-competition (step 0) onward but only defined in evaluating-market-structures (step 3, last subsection). IAL orders Efficiency (3.3.1) before the structures. The 'Spectrum of Market Structures' overview exists in notes[0] but not in content[], so Learn Mode opens cold on perfect competition with no map of the four structures.

Pre-test gate: 3 random MCQs from a 12-item bank in which 4 items (shutdown point, natural monopoly, monopsony, barrier types) test material absent from content[]; P(at least one untaught item) = 1 − C(8,3)/C(12,3) ≈ 75%. This directly feeds the founder's 'pre-test demotivates' hypothesis for this section.

Pairing coherence is otherwise fine: (PC, mon comp), (kinked, game theory), (monopoly, PD), (contestability, efficiency evaluation). Block 3 takeaway[2] ('statically inefficient but dynamically efficient') previews block 4's content rather than summarising block 3 — minor. Difficulty ramp is sensible; monopoly-before-oligopoly would be the more conventional order but the current one works.

Misconceptions are genuine student errors (normal ≠ zero profit; monopolistic competition ≠ monopoly; oligopoly ≠ always high prices; collusion ≠ always succeeds; PD ≠ always harmful; contestable ≠ merely low entry barriers). 'monopolies always bad' (monopoly-equilibrium-welfare) and 'PC always ideal' (evaluating-market-structures) overlap and could be differentiated (e.g. replace the latter with 'students draw monopoly price from the MR curve').

Real examples are 100% UK (wheat aside): Tesco/Sainsbury's/Asda/Morrisons, Thames Water/Ofwat, Avanti West Coast, CMA, Ryanair/easyJet. For the stated audience (HK, Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Middle East) none of these are recognisable; IAL examiners accept any country's examples.
Monopsony (IAL 3.3 'Monopsony'): characteristics; costs and benefits to firms, consumers, employees and suppliers — entirely absent from content[], notes[] and flashcards, though quiz[9] tests it.
Natural monopoly (under Monopoly): continuously falling LRAC, MES vs market size, why competition is wasteful — absent from content[] (only in quiz[6] and practice[2] guidance).
Efficiency (IAL 3.3 'Efficiency'): X-inefficiency is never defined or taught; efficiency definitions only appear in the last subsection rather than framing the section.
Oligopoly: calculation and interpretation of n-firm concentration ratios — absent from content[] (defined once in notes[3]).
Oligopoly: types of price competition — price wars, predatory pricing, limit pricing — absent (limit pricing appears only as quiz[10]'s answer).
Oligopoly: non-price competition (advertising, branding, loyalty schemes, quality) and reasons firms prefer it — absent (one 'link' line in notes[2]).
Oligopoly: overt vs tacit collusion and the factors making collusion more/less likely (number of firms, similar costs, stable demand, detection/enforcement) — only lightly touched.
Monopoly: costs and benefits of monopoly to firms, employees and suppliers (spec asks for all stakeholder groups) — only consumers/society covered.
Monopoly: third-degree price discrimination diagram and explicit costs/benefits to producers AND consumers — evaluation is present, diagram is absent.
Contestability: types of barriers to entry and exit (legal, sunk costs, economies of scale, brand loyalty, predatory behaviour) — no taxonomy of barriers taught anywhere in content[].

Perfect competition: short-run loss-making equilibrium and shutdown decision (P ≥ AVC) — not in content[] (may belong to the revenue-costs-profits section; unsure of IAL placement, but quiz[2] tests it here).

Unsure: the kinked demand curve is given a full subsection and diagram, but I do not recall it as an explicit IAL oligopoly bullet (the explicit bullets are concentration ratios, collusive/non-collusive behaviour, game theory, price and non-price competition). Worth verifying against the WEC13 spec before keeping it at this weight.

Unsure: app numbering '3.3.3' does not correspond to IAL spec numbering, where Market structures and contestability is its own topic heading with ~7 sub-bullets (Efficiency, Perfect competition, Monopolistic competition, Oligopoly, Monopoly, Monopsony, Contestability); the app's 3.3.1/3.3.2 are Business growth and Revenues/costs.

Add diagramRef/quizIndices/practiceIndices to all three blocks (block 0: 'Competitive Labour Market', quiz [0,1], practice [0]; block 1: 'Monopsony', quiz [5,6], practice [3]; block 2: 'Wage Differentials', quiz [7,8,9], practice [1,4]) so the monopsony diagram actually renders and inline MCQs/practice match what was just taught.

Write recalls for all six subsections — reorder for the monopsony construction (faces whole market supply → must raise wage for all → MCL above S → hire where MCL = MRP → pay wage from S), reorder for NMW-in-monopsony, fillin for 'MRP = MPP × MR; hire until MRP = W', fillin for bilateral monopoly/indeterminate wage.

Fix wage-differentials keyIdea ('not because markets are failing') and add a short NMW-in-competitive-market paragraph plus determinants of elasticity of demand/supply for labour, so the misconceptions and quiz[2] rest on taught content.
Repair the two monopsony SVGs: put Wm on the supply curve, Qc at the true S=MRP intersection, Qmin at the Wmin ∩ S kink, and correct the 'Wmin = MRP' construction note.

Bring practice in line with IAL command words and marking: Define → 2 marks (or 'Explain', 4); drop 'Outline'; make the 20-mark guidance total 20, structure as KAA/Evaluation levels, and require the monopsony diagram.

content[2] 'Trade Unions and Wage Differentials' > wage-differentials > keyIdea: States wages differ 'not because markets are failing'. The IAL spec explicitly lists geographical and occupational immobility as market failure in labour markets, and the same section's own body calls discrimination 'unjustified' and immobility a 'friction' that stops differentials being competed away. A student who writes 'wage differentials are not a market failure' in an exam loses the evaluation.

q2: Correct (index 2) and distractors are fine, but the determinants of elasticity of demand for labour are not taught in any content[] subsection. Because no block has quizIndices, the legacy fallback (components/learn-mode/utils.js distributeItems) shows quiz[0], quiz[1], quiz[2] at steps 0/1/2, so this untaught question is the inline MCQ on the Trade Unions & Wage Differentials step.

No block has diagramRef, quizIndices or practiceIndices, so LearnModeTab.jsx:86 takes the legacy fallback. matchDiagramsToBlocks (utils.js:31) scores by title-word overlap: 'Competitive Labour Market Equilibrium' matches block 0 ('Demand and Supply of Labour') on 'labour' and consumes it; 'Monopsony Labour Market' then scores 0 against 'Wage Determination' and 'Trade Unions and Wage Differentials' and is NEVER shown. The single most examined diagram in the section is invisible in Learn Mode.

distributeItems fallback assigns quiz[0], quiz[1], quiz[2] to steps 0/1/2: step 1 (monopsony) gets the MRP = W question, step 2 (unions/differentials) gets the untaught elasticity question. quiz[5..9] (monopsony, NMW, differentials, immobility) never appear inline.

Practice fallback sorts by marks then takes the first three: step 0 = Define derived demand (worked), step 1 = Outline trade unions (guided) — shown BEFORE trade unions are taught in step 2 — and step 2 = Explain wage differentials. The Assess (10) and Evaluate (20) questions never reach Learn Mode.

Zero recall objects across all six subsections: the spaced/immediate recall mechanism has nothing to show, so the only retrieval in the whole section is three inline MCQs. This section has several genuinely orderable chains that should be recalls (monopsony construction; NMW-in-monopsony mechanism; derived-demand chain; union wage above equilibrium → move up MRP → lower employment).

Block 2 pairing is incoherent: 'Trade Unions' is the bilateral-monopoly counterpart to monopsony and belongs with block 1; 'Wage Differentials' belongs with supply-side immobility. Suggested: Block 1 = competitive market + NMW in a competitive market; Block 2 = monopsony + trade unions/bilateral monopoly; Block 3 = wage differentials + immobility + government policy.

Firm vs market never distinguished: no subsection shows the perfectly competitive firm facing a horizontal labour supply (W = ACL = MCL) hiring where W = MRP, so the jump to 'MCL above supply' in monopsony has no baseline diagram to contrast against.

NMW in a COMPETITIVE labour market (wage floor → excess supply → unemployment) is never taught, yet monopsony-power > misconception refers to 'the standard unemployment prediction' as if it had been, and flashcard 'What is the national minimum wage' states it. The student meets the exception before the rule.

trade-unions > body flow is a list of three parallel cases (competitive / monopsony / bilateral monopoly), not a causal chain — misuse of the flow type; would confuse a reorder recall if one were later generated from it.

demand-for-labour-mrp > misconception ('firms hire workers because they need them') is filler. Real student errors here: confusing a movement along MRP (wage change) with a shift (product demand / productivity); writing MRP = MPP × price when the product market is imperfectly competitive; treating diminishing returns as workers being 'worse'.

supply-of-labour > examMatters directly contradicts the Notes-tab examMatters for the same subsection (backward-bending 'favourite diagram' vs 'most questions focus on the market supply curve'). Students switching tabs see opposite advice.
Difficulty ramp is otherwise sensible (demand/supply → competitive → monopsony → unions → differentials) and each block's takeaway list faithfully summarises its two subsections.
Elasticity of demand for labour and its determinants (labour share of cost, substitutability, PED of product, time) — not taught; tested in quiz[2].
Elasticity of supply of labour and its determinants (training period, qualifications, mobility, time) — not taught beyond one sentence.
National minimum wage in a competitive labour market (wage floor, excess supply, unemployment diagram) — only the monopsony case is covered.

Government intervention to reduce labour market failure: maximum wages, public-sector wage setting, policies to tackle geographical/occupational immobility (housing, retraining, relocation grants) — only appears in quiz[9].

Current labour market issues listed in WEC13 3.4.3 (from my recollection of the spec — treat as 'probable'): skills shortages, ageing population/retirement age, young workers, flexible/temporary/zero-hours working, migration — only migration is touched, via one flow and one misconception.

content.text: Diagram for the individual firm in a perfectly competitive labour market (horizontal supply to the firm, W = MRP) versus the industry — not taught.
Discrimination as a labour-market failure — one sentence only; no analysis of how it distorts demand for labour.

Unsure: whether WEC13 explicitly requires MRP = MPP × MR theory (the 2018 spec wording I recall is 'demand for labour as derived demand' plus factors influencing demand). Content leans heavily on MRP; not wrong, but examMatters 'Examiners expect you to draw the MRP curve' may overclaim.

Section numbering: the app labels this 3.3.4; in the WEC13 spec I recall the labour market as topic 3.4 (3.4.1 demand, 3.4.2 supply, 3.4.3 wage determination). Unsure — flag for verification against the current spec PDF.

content.text: Add recall exercises to every subsection (currently zero): a reorder for the integration ladder (FTA > customs union > common market > monetary union), fillins for trade creation vs diversion and for the four causes of globalisation, and a fillin for TNC motives; and set diagramRef/quizIndices/practiceIndices on each block so inline widgets match the block.

Give the Trade Blocs block its own assessment: at least 3 MCQs (FTA vs CU, trade creation vs diversion scenario, effect of a lower CET), one 'Explain'/'Examine' practice question, and either a real trade creation/diversion diagram or delete the 'show it on a diagram' instruction in examMatters.

Fix the content errors: Brexit realExample ('lost tariff-free access' is false; TCA is zero-tariff), define trade diversion by preferential tariff removal rather than 'the CET forces', add the spec term 'common market', and introduce TNC = MNC in block 2 so the quiz/practice vocabulary matches the notes.

Repair diagram 1 (FDI reasons/impacts): the Reasons column and the Positive-impacts column overlap (x 60-140, y 153-257) and render on top of each other; and either source real indexed data for diagram 0 or remove its numeric gridlines.

Rewrite practice guidance in IAL levels form (KAA/Evaluation split, e.g. 6/4 for 10-mark Assess, 12/8 for 20-mark Evaluate), replace 'Outline' with 'Explain', cut 'Define... (4 marks)' to 2 marks, and add an 8-mark 'Examine' item so the set mirrors a Section B ladder.

Trade Blocs > trade-creation-diversion > realExample: States 'After Brexit, the UK lost tariff-free access to EU markets'. Wrong: the UK-EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement (in force 1 Jan 2021) keeps zero tariffs and zero quotas on goods meeting rules of origin. What the UK lost was frictionless access (customs declarations, rules-of-origin checks, SPS and regulatory non-tariff barriers). The 'trade diversion in reverse' framing is also muddled and not a term a marker will recognise.

Trade Blocs > trade-creation-diversion > examMatters: Tells students to 'Show trade creation and diversion on a diagram', but the section contains no such diagram (the 3 diagrams are an indicators line chart, an FDI flow chart and a costs/benefits balance). Students are told to do something the section never teaches.

diagrams[1] 'FDI Flows: Reasons and Impacts' (svg): Layout bug: the 'Reasons for FDI' column occupies x=10-140, y=100-257, while the 'Positive (+)' impact boxes occupy x=60-230, y=153-273. They overlap in the region x=60-140, y=153-257, so four reason labels and four positive-impact labels render on top of each other and the diagram is unreadable.

Zero recall exercises (meta.reorder=0, meta.fillin=0): Learn Mode's 'spaced' top-of-step and 'immediate' bottom-of-step retrieval widgets never appear in this section. Obvious candidates exist: reorder = the integration ladder FTA > customs union > common market > monetary union (genuine sequence); fillin = trade creation/diversion definitions; fillin = the four causes of globalisation.

No block carries diagramRef, quizIndices or practiceIndices, so InlineDiagram/InlineQuiz/InlinePractice cannot be matched to the block being studied; whatever fallback the code uses, block 3 (Trade Blocs) has no quiz MCQ, practice question or diagram anywhere in the section, so its end-of-block widgets are necessarily off-topic.

Trade Blocs block is placed under 'Causes and Effects of Globalisation' (spec 4.1) although the IAL spec puts trading blocs and the WTO under 'Trade and the global economy' (app section 4.3.2, which currently has no trade-bloc block). A student revising by spec point will not find trade blocs where the spec puts them; either move the block or cross-reference it in both places.

Each block has exactly two subsections, so the whole section is 3 steps; a 6-subsection, 3-step section with no recalls is very thin for a topic that carries a 20-mark essay. Blocks 1 and 2 could each gain a third subsection (block 1: characteristics/indicators of globalisation, which quiz[0] and diagram 0 assume; block 2: the type-of-FDI distinction greenfield vs M&A that common_mistakes[1] relies on).

Quiz and extras test vocabulary the content body never introduces: 'race to the bottom' (quiz 4, 8; practice 3 guidance; extras), 'characteristics of globalisation' (quiz 0), 'greenfield vs M&A FDI' (common_mistakes[1]), 'TNC' (all quiz/practice). Learn Mode students hit these cold.

Misconception quality is mixed: types-of-trade-bloc (FTA vs customs union = CET) is the classic real error and is well handled; benefits-costs ('entirely good or entirely bad') and costs-of-mncs ('MNCs are always bad') are the same generic 'be balanced' filler stated twice. The notes[] misconception for the same subsection ('students treat globalisation as entirely new') is a different, better one and is not surfaced in Learn Mode.

Stakeholder framing absent: IAL question stems ask for impact on 'governments', 'producers', 'workers', 'consumers', 'the environment'; the content is organised as benefits vs costs with governments and producers never addressed as stakeholders (diagram 2's 'TNC influence on policy' is the only mention of governments).

Takeaways match their blocks well and the ramp (causes > effects > MNC benefits > MNC costs > bloc types > creation/diversion) is sensible; the 2-per-step pairs are coherent (each pair is a benefit/cost or definition/application couple). This is the section's structural strength.
Characteristics of globalisation (rising trade/GDP, FDI and capital flows, TNC growth, migration, integration of financial markets): not taught in content body; only implied by quiz[0] and diagram 0.

Impact of globalisation on governments (tax competition/'race to the bottom', reduced policy autonomy, tax base erosion) and on producers (access to larger markets, cheaper inputs, global supply chains, competition): spec lists impacts on 'individual countries, governments, producers and consumers, workers and the environment'; governments and producers are not covered as stakeholders.
Growth of TNCs as a factor contributing to globalisation (spec lists TNCs among the causes): TNCs appear only as an effect/actor in block 2; practice[1] asks it but the body never teaches it.
Deindustrialisation in developed economies as an effect (flashcards teach it; content body does not).
'Common market' as the spec term for the third level of integration, and 'economic union' as a level: absent (unsure whether IAL requires economic union explicitly).
Trade creation and trade diversion diagram: examMatters demands it, none provided. Unsure whether the IAL spec requires the diagram, but the concepts sit under spec 4.2 trading blocs, not 4.1.
Brain drain / migration effects on source and host countries: flashcards mention brain drain; content body only mentions migration in a misconception (unsure whether IAL 4.1 or 4.5 expects this).

Add the missing content: a real 'International Competitiveness' section pair (measures: relative ULC and relative export prices; factors; significance) and an 'Effects of Exchange Rate Changes' section (inflation, growth, employment, FDI, competitive devaluation, revaluation/devaluation terminology), plus 'Correcting a current account deficit' in block 1. This makes quiz[5..11] and practice[4] teachable and closes ~8 spec bullets.

Wire the blocks into Learn Mode: add diagramRef ('Balance of Payments Structure' on block 1; 'Exchange Rate Determination' on block 2, J-curve on the new effects block) and quizIndices/practiceIndices so inline quiz and practice match what the step taught.

Add recall widgets from existing flows: reorder on 'Imports exceed exports -> CA deficit -> financed by financial account surplus -> capital inflows' and 'Fed raises rates -> capital attracted -> demand for $ rises -> $ appreciates'; fillin on '|PED_x| + |PED_m| > __' with word bank {exports, imports, 1, 0}.

Fix precision errors: three BoP accounts (not two) in body[0]/keyIdea; 'sum of elasticities < 1' instead of 'inelastic on both sides' in the ML paragraph; replace the Brexit 'textbook J-curve' example with an international one (Sri Lanka 2022 or Turkey 2018-21) worded as 'consistent with'.

Realign practice to IAL conventions: Define 2 marks, Explain 4, Analyse 6, Assess 10/12, Evaluate 14/20; drop 'Outline'; rewrite guidance for the 10- and 20-markers as levels descriptors (KAA + Evaluation) rather than point tallies, and state the diagram expected.

content[1] 'Competitiveness' > marshall-lerner-j-curve > realExample: Claims post-Brexit sterling depreciation produced 'a textbook J-curve' with UK exports 'gradually becoming more competitive' over two years. The UK current account deficit actually narrowed sharply in late 2016 (5.2% of GDP in 2016 to ~3.5% in 2017, driven largely by primary income valuation effects), and the widely discussed empirical finding is the absence of an export volume response (exporters raised sterling prices/margins). Presenting a contested, arguably counter-example as 'textbook' is misleading; a teacher who knows the data will object.
q7: Unit labour costs never appear in content[]. Block 2 is titled 'Competitiveness' but has no competitiveness content. Question and explanation are correct.

p4: 'Outline two measures ... (4 marks)': 'Outline' is not an IAL Economics command word (should be 'Explain'). The topic (measures of competitiveness) is not taught anywhere in content[]. Guidance uses 'real effective exchange rate' where the spec bullet 4.3.3(a) names 'relative export prices' and 'relative unit labour costs'; REER is acceptable but the spec term should appear.

Block 2 is titled 'Competitiveness' (content[1].title) but its two sections are exchange-rate-determination and marshall-lerner-j-curve; there is no section on international competitiveness. Its takeaways do not mention competitiveness either. Retitle to 'Exchange Rate Movements and Their Effects' and add a genuine competitiveness block.

Zero recall widgets in a section with two genuine causal chains already written as flow blocks (balance-of-payments flow: imports exceed exports -> CA deficit -> financed by financial account surplus -> capital inflows; exchange-rate-determination flow: Fed raises rates -> capital attracted -> demand for dollars rises -> dollar appreciates). Both are ideal reorder recalls; ML condition is an ideal fillin ('|PED_ + PED_| > _'). Learn Mode currently offers no retrieval practice at all.

Neither block has a diagramRef (content[0] and content[1] keys are title/sections/takeaway only), although diagrams[] contains five relevant diagrams including the currency-market S/D diagram that examMatters explicitly tells students to draw. If InlineDiagram matches by diagramRef substring, no diagram is ever shown in Learn Mode for this section. Add diagramRef 'Balance of Payments Structure' to block 1 and 'Exchange Rate Determination' (or 'J-Curve') to block 2.

No quizIndices/practiceIndices on either block, so the inline quiz/practice at the end of block 1 (BoP + systems) may draw ML/ULC questions the student has not reached, and the pre-test draws 3 of 12 where 6 test untaught material.

Replace quiz[5] (Laffer), quiz[6] (occupational immobility), quiz[7] (poverty trap) with on-spec MCQs on mergers/SLC, predatory pricing vs abuse of dominance, and quality standards/performance targets; then add quizIndices, practiceIndices and diagramRef to each block so pre-test and inline items match what the step teaches.

Fix the diagrams: redraw diagrams[0] as a natural-monopoly price-cap diagram (falling LRAC, P=MC vs P=AC caps, Preg not below AC, MC=MR dashed lines at the true intersection); retitle/replace diagrams[2] so privatisation is not shown as a competitive supply shift; add the competitive-market NMW diagram the examMatters demands; draw the kinked post-NMW MCL in diagrams[1].

Add the missing spec content as a new block ('Promoting competition and contestability': deregulation, competitive tendering, promotion of small business; 'Protecting suppliers': monopsony buyers) plus a short 'impact on prices, profit, efficiency, quality, choice' summary table; consider moving the minimum-wage subsection to 3.3.4.
